title: Lane Kiffin backed Trinidad Chambliss' extra year — until the QB stayed at Ole Miss
description: Ahead of Lane Kiffin's return to Ole Miss, new book reveals LSU football coach's pursuit of Rebels stars Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy.
content: Lane Kiffin backed Trinidad Chambliss' extra year — until QB stayed at Ole Miss The boos will come Saturday night. So will the resentment. When Lane Kiffin jogs into Vaught-Hemingway Stadium for the first time as LSU's coach, he won't be returning as a beloved former coach getting a standing ovation. He'll be returning as the man Ole Miss fans believe left them at the altar. Kiffin walked away with Ole Miss preparing for the first College Football Playoff run in school history. The departure left behind hard feelings that remain very much alive in Oxford. It wasn't just that Kiffin left. It was what happened next. As detailed in John Talty's forthcoming biography, Lane Being Lane: The Story of Lane Kiffin, College Football's Agent of Chaos, Kiffin wasn't merely moving on to LSU. He was actively attempting to bring key Ole Miss players with him, including quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, whose unexpected rise helped fuel the Rebels' playoff run. According to attorney Tom Mars, Kiffin became intensely invested in Chambliss' eligibility appeal, frequently checking for updates and making little effort to disguise why. Ultimately, Ole Miss fought off LSU's pursuit. The Rebels convinced Chambliss to stay, retained star running back Kewan Lacy and advanced into the playoff under new coach Pete Golding. But the episode only deepened the divide between Kiffin and the program he left behind. Now the architect of that chaos returns to Oxford with a top-10 LSU team, national championship aspirations and a spotlight he has never exactly tried to avoid. The college football world already would've been watching. Talty's reporting adds another layer to a game that was personal long before kickoff. *** Three days before Ole Miss’s home playoff game against Tulane, Tom Mars got a curious voicemail. “Tom, this is Lane. Please call me.” Mars, a former general counsel for Walmart, had never talked to Lane Kiffin before in his life. He was aware of him, obviously, but wasn’t sure the message was even authentic. When he checked with a friend that the phone number was really Kiffin’s, he became intrigued about what the new LSU head coach wanted. Over the phone, Kiffin explained to him the Trinidad Chambliss situation. Chambliss became a national revelation in his lone season at Ole Miss after he replaced an injured Austin Simmons and never let go of the starting job. There was something special about Chambliss that seemed to make everyone around him better. Despite not starting the first two games, he finished the season with 3,937 passing yards and 22 touchdowns. Chambliss was trying for another year of eligibility but was facing an NCAA hurdle. Mars had developed a reputation as a bulldog attorney who wasn’t afraid to grapple with the NCAA, privately or publicly. Interestingly, he had previously represented former Ole Miss coach Houston Nutt and played a role in the Hugh Freeze escort scandal when his diligent review of Freeze’s phone records turned up inappropriate calls. Had that never happened, who knows if Kiffin ever would have ended up at Ole Miss in the first place. Kiffin said Chambliss was a great kid who could really use outside help to put pressure on the NCAA to do the right thing. After reviewing the case and talking with Ole Miss compliance director Taylor Hall, Mars agreed to take on Chambliss’s cause. At the time, Ole Miss had already appealed the NCAA’s initial denial of the school’s waiver request which hinged on Chambliss missing the 2022 season at Division-II Ferris State due to complications around tonsillitis. As Mars put together his strategy, Kiffin wanted near constant updates on where things stood. He’d text or call Mars several times a day. It was beyond unique for a rival head coach to be that invested in trying to get a player an extra year of eligibility, even if it was a former player. But Lane didn’t even try to hide his true intentions. “It was clear to me — it’d be clear to anyone except the village idiot — that he was hoping the appeal would be granted so he could bring Trinidad to LSU,” says Mars. Mars enjoyed his conversations with the LSU head coach. The more they talked, the more open Kiffin became with him about what he was trying to do. With the transfer portal soon to open, time was of the essence for him. Kiffin knew he needed a transfer portal quarterback and Chambliss was his preferred pick, but he couldn’t afford to wait long on him. If Chambliss couldn’t get his appeal approved in time, he’d have to move on to his other top targets because of how fast the transfer portal quarterback market would move. He repeatedly asked the lawyer for his educated opinion on the likelihood that the NCAA would grant Chambliss’ appeal. Eventually, Kiffin told Mars if the NCAA didn’t “declare him eligible by that weekend, then I’ve got to go get somebody else.” *** Ole Miss knew what Kiffin was up to. It knew that he badly wanted to steal Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy. And it knew he was using running backs coach Kevin Smith as his proxy to stay in Lacy’s ear, especially about leaving for LSU. Pete Golding, Keith Carter and Grove Collective executive director Walker Jones acted decisively to prevent that from happening. First, it convinced Chambliss to stay. It would be pending a successful NCAA appeal, but Ole Miss could afford to wait out that process in a way that Kiffin couldn’t. Ole Miss finalized a late-night deal with Chambliss — “It was an all-night process. It’s crazy what happens after midnight,” says Walker Jones. LSU pivoted to Arizona State transfer Sam Leavitt. Having Chambliss on board was key, but so was the comfort Lacy felt in Oxford. He trusted Golding and others to deliver on their promises. “The biggest thing is we didn’t panic, we didn’t get desperate,” Jones says. “We trusted what those guys were telling us. We also trusted that we had done right by those guys. We had done right by Trinidad, we had done right by Kewan… and we treated them with respect and we listened to them.” Lane was the one who roped Tom Mars into Chambliss’s NCAA appeal, but once he knew that the quarterback was staying in Oxford, his tone changed. After initially selling Mars on what a great kid Chambliss was and why he deserved another season, Lane now scoffed that the quarterback only had a sore throat. Lane even called Mars one day and claimed that he and Chambliss would lose their Mississippi court case. “After the portal, the switch flipped,” says Mars. “There weren’t any encouraging messages. Mostly sarcastic. I thought it was kind of fun.” Excerpted from the book “Lane Being Lane: The Story of Lane Kiffin, College Football’s Agent of Chaos.” From Harper Books. Reprinted with permission.

title: How much of the current market movement is linked to the CLARITY Act vote?
description: Crypto markets weakened after the US Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act, but the selloff came amid a broader risk-off environment. Bitcoin fell around 3-4%, while crypto-linked equities saw sharper declines. The regulatory setback added pressure, but el…
content: The Senate vote was significant. The CLARITY Act failed to clear the procedural threshold, with a 50-49 vote falling short of the 60 votes required to advance it. The setback removes the prospect of Congress delivering a comprehensive market-structure framework for digital assets in 2026. The market reaction also tells us something important about how investors view different parts of the crypto ecosystem. That divergence suggests that the regulatory outcome may have been particularly important for companies whose business models and valuations had incorporated expectations of clearer US market rules. For Bitcoin itself, the relationship is less direct. Bitcoin already has a more established regulatory and legal position than many newer digital assets. What we can say is that CLARITY clearly amplified the pressure on crypto, particularly on crypto-related equities. But the broader market environment was already challenging. Global bond yields have been elevated, increasing the relative attractiveness of yield-bearing assets. Oil prices have also remained a source of inflationary pressure, reinforcing concerns around monetary policy. These factors affect Bitcoin and other risk assets regardless of what happens in Washington. Interestingly, on-chain indicators offer a more mixed picture than price action alone suggests. Bitcoin's realised cap has returned to growth after an extended period of contraction, while short-term holders have recently remained in aggregate profit. CryptoQuant data therefore points to a market that is under pressure, but not necessarily one showing uniform signs of capitulation. What happens next? The failure of the CLARITY Act does not necessarily mean the regulatory conversation ends. It changes the route through which that clarity could emerge. One possibility is greater reliance on SEC and CFTC rulemaking. The agencies have already demonstrated that they can provide additional guidance within their existing mandates, and the SEC and CFTC's March 2026 interpretation was explicitly positioned as a step toward greater clarity while Congress considers broader legislation. The legislative route also remains possible in the longer term, although the current version now faces a much more uncertain path. For markets, the immediate question may therefore be less about the fate of one bill and more about whether regulatory clarity continues to improve through other channels. The bigger lesson from this move is that crypto's sensitivity to US regulation is changing. Bitcoin increasingly trades as a global macro asset, while regulatory developments can have a much more differentiated impact across exchanges, stablecoin issuers, crypto-linked companies and individual tokens. That means investors should be careful about treating every crypto market move as a referendum on regulation. The current episode is better understood as a meaningful regulatory setback arriving in an already fragile macro environment. The next phase will depend on which path gains momentum. Whether it’s legislation, agency rulemaking, or a combination of both. Until that becomes clearer, volatility is likely to reflect both the regulatory debate and the broader global liquidity environment. content: MDA CHORUS™ COMMAND, MDA CHORUS™ COMMAND PRO and MDA CHORUS™ INTELLIGENCE provide customers end-to-end control of their Earth observation workflow TORONTO and PARIS, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MDA Space Ltd. (TSX: MDA) (NYSE: MDA), a trusted mission partner to the global defence and space industry, unveiled today at the World Space Business Week conference the end-to-end MDA CHORUS™ Earth observation (EO) product portfolio. The introduction of the full portfolio precedes the highly anticipated launch of the MDA CHORUS™ constellation later this year. Leveraging the company's next generation MDA CHORUS™ constellation, the introduction of MDA CHORUS™ COMMAND, MDA CHORUS™ COMMAND PRO and MDA CHORUS™ INTELLIGENCE offers customers a complete portfolio to customize, manage and control their geointelligence workflow — from data collection planning to tasking to decision-ready insight. "Earth observation at MDA Space has always meant more than building world-class spacecraft. We have spent decades turning synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data into intelligence products for maritime, defence and critical infrastructure monitoring" said Mike Greenley, CEO of MDA Space. "With this new expanded MDA CHORUS™ product line, we have taken that same heritage and built it into a user-friendly and complete product system that customers can directly access, task, and grow with." A Complete Earth Observation System, Built Around the Customer Incorporating constellation assets, ground infrastructure, archive access and analytics, the MDA CHORUS™ product portfolio now provides customers a complete unified commercial architecture, including: MDA CHORUS™ COMMAND: The operational entry point for the ecosystem, this intuitive platform allows customers to search the archive, define areas of interest, set imaging priorities, tip and cue, and schedule acquisitions. It includes Application Programming Interface (API) connectors, guides and a knowledge hub, streamlining and consolidating customer access to MDA CHORUS™. MDA CHORUS™ COMMAND PRO: Enables maximum customer control of the system by integrating an MDA CHORUS™ regional ground station directly into a customer's operations, providing direct downlink and near-real-time local processing — eliminating latency and delivering the independence that defence and critical infrastructure customers require. MDA CHORUS™ INTELLIGENCE: A comprehensive suite of geointelligence data and analytics products leveraging decades of SAR expertise and spanning maritime awareness, vessel detection, oil-on-water, ground deformation and energy infrastructure monitoring. The suite draws on SAR satellite images and telemetry, value-added geographic information system (GIS) data files and reports, and integrated third-party data products. MDA CHORUS™ Constellation: Powering the portfolio is the MDA CHORUS™ Constellation, a three satellite system fully integrating two new spacecraft — one X-band, one C-band — delivering high-revisit, all-weather imaging on orbit, anchored by RADARSAT-2, the company's world-leading EO platform already on orbit. Today's product announcement builds on the official opening last month of the company's new MDA CHORUS™ Control Centre, marking another operational readiness milestone as momentum builds for the constellation's launch in late 2026. title: ‘Vivant’ Tops Asia Streaming Chart, First Japanese Drama to Lead, Report Finds
description: TBS drama “Vivant” outdrew every other streaming title across Asia last month, excluding China and India, becoming the first Japanese show to top ampd Analytics’ regional monthly ranking since the measurement firm began tracking the market. The finding comes …
content: TBS drama “Vivant” outdrew every other streaming title across Asia last month, excluding China and India, becoming the first Japanese show to top ampd Analytics’ regional monthly ranking since the measurement firm began tracking the market. The finding comes from a new ampd Vision report titled “Vivant: A TV Broadcast Hit, Streamed.” “Vivant,” which launched its second season in July as part of TBS’s Sunday Theater slot, pulled in 15.6 million unique viewers regionwide in August, with 15.1 million watching in Japan alone. That figure equals a quarter of the 61.4 million viewers ampd tracks across Japanese VOD, according to the report from ampd Analytics, the streaming measurement arm of Media Partners Asia (MPA). The series follows Yusuke Nogi, a Japanese trading company employee drawn into an international conspiracy tied to a shadowy government intelligence unit known as Beppan. Season 2 picks up immediately after the first season’s cliffhanger and was shot partly on location in Azerbaijan. Popular on Variety Much of that reach came through TVer, the free platform operated by Japan’s broadcast networks, which drew 10.2 million of the show’s viewers. Only two other titles have ever pulled 10 million viewers on one platform in a single market within a month, according to ampd: broadcasts of the World Baseball Classic in Japan and the Korean drama “Teach You a Lesson,” both distributed on Netflix. TBS made the new season available on TVer at no cost within an hour of its Sunday broadcast, reserving paid streaming exclusively for U-Next. That arrangement created a second viewing peak each week, on Monday nights, and 92% of viewers who came back for a new episode had already watched the previous one by the time it aired. The show’s popularity also lifted viewership of its first season elsewhere. Netflix’s audience for “Vivant” grew more than eightfold between May and August, from 300,000 viewers to 2.5 million, while U-Next’s viewership rose over the same period from 100,000 to 2 million. That shift happened even among subscribers who already had access to the show elsewhere: an estimated one in eight Prime Video subscribers and one in 10 Netflix subscribers in Japan chose to watch “Vivant” on TVer rather than on the services they already pay for. Beyond the streaming platforms, “Vivant” built a substantial following on YouTube, where related content drew 13.2 million viewers, nearly matching its VOD reach. That audience was spread across more than 1,600 videos posted by 450 channels, totaling 8.8 million hours watched at an average of almost 40 minutes per viewer. A companion show TBS produced alongside the drama, “Villains’ Meeting Room,” averaged more than 1.3 million viewers an episode. “‘Vivant’ is a distribution story as much as a content story,” said Sam Yousif, managing director of ampd Analytics. “A quarter of Japan’s tracked VOD audience watched one drama in a single month, and premium subscribers moved to a free platform to follow it. Japan is the largest VOD market we measure, with the closest relationship between broadcast and streaming anywhere in the region, and measuring a title today means measuring it everywhere it lives, including YouTube, where ‘Vivant’ reached almost as many people as it did on VOD.” The drama’s success did not extend much beyond Japan’s borders. Some 97% of all “Vivant” viewing came from local audiences, ampd found, a pattern consistent with Japanese dramas’ broader struggles abroad: they land in Netflix’s global top 10 outside Japan just 0.3 times a month on average, well behind Korean dramas at 4.1 times and Japanese anime at 1.4.

title: India to add 3,860 MW data centre capacity by 2030, require USD 29.9 bn investment: Report - The Tribune
description: India's data centre sector is set for a major capacity expansion, with 3,860 MW of new capacity expected to come up by 2030, including 509 MW already under construction and 3,351 MW in the planning stage, according to a report by Cushman & Wakefield.
content: New Delhi [India], September 16 (ANI): India's data centre sector is set for a major capacity expansion, with 3,860 MW of new capacity expected to come up by 2030, including 509 MW already under construction and 3,351 MW in the planning stage, according to a report by Cushman & Wakefield. The expansion is expected to require USD 29.9 billion in development capital through 2030, placing India among the major data centre investment markets in the Asia Pacific region, the report said. India's operational data centre capacity stood at 1,789 MW as of H1 2026, up from around 400 MW in 2019. The country's top seven markets added 178 MW of capacity during the first half of 2026, while colocation vacancy stood at 14.9%. Mumbai remains the country's largest data centre market, accounting for 50% of operational capacity at 890 MW. It also has the largest upcoming pipeline at around 1.7 GW as of H1 2026, with the city expected to cross 1 GW of operational capacity by end-2026, the report said. However, capacity expansion is increasingly spreading across other major hubs. Hyderabad has 151 MW of operational capacity and 710 MW of upcoming supply, while Chennai has 214 MW operational capacity and 368 MW of upcoming supply. Delhi NCR has 183 MW operational capacity and 387 MW of future supply. The report said India's relatively low data centre penetration, growing enterprise use of artificial intelligence and increasing hyperscaler activity leave significant room for future expansion. It also noted that AI-focused infrastructure is driving demand for facilities with higher rack densities. Cushman & Wakefield Executive Managing Director Gautam Saraf said, “With nearly 3.9 GW of additional capacity expected across the country's leading markets by 2030, this deeper ecosystem will be critical in supporting the next phase of cloud adoption, AI deployment and data-driven growth across the economy.” At the Asia Pacific level, data centre capacity is projected to increase 2.7 times by 2030, requiring more than USD 280 billion in capital expenditure. India is expected to account for nearly USD 29.9 billion of this development investment, the report said. The report also flagged sustainability as an increasing planning priority, as the rapid expansion of AI workloads is expected to raise data centre energy demand and resource requirements. (ANI) (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

title: (PHOTO) Owala's New Pokemon Water Bottles Land at Target for the Franchise's Big 30th Anniversary Bash
description: Owala is releasing five Pokémon-themed FreeSip water bottles exclusively at Target to mark Pokémon's 30th anniversary, with designs featuring several of the franchise's best-known characters.
content: Drinkware brand Owala is releasing a new collection of Pokemon-themed water bottles exclusively at Target on Wednesday, timing the launch to coincide with the video game franchise's 30th anniversary celebrations. The Owala x Pokemon collection features five distinct FreeSip water bottle designs built around some of the franchise's most recognizable characters. Confirmed designs include a bright yellow, cream and blue bottle centered on Pikachu, marketed as the "Pikachu I Choose You" edition, alongside separate bottles dedicated to Charizard and Gengar, a design featuring Eevee alongside its evolved forms Sylveon and Vaporeon, and a Kanto Starter Trio bottle bringing together Bulbasaur, Charmander and Squirtle. Owala gave fans an early look at the collection through a short video posted to Instagram ahead of the official release, showcasing the designs across the lineup. Owala's FreeSip bottles, the format used across the new Pokemon collection, are known for a two-way spout system that lets users drink either upright through an integrated straw or tilt the bottle back to use a wider opening. The stainless steel bottles also feature insulated construction, a leak-resistant push-button lid, and a carry loop that doubles as a lock when closed, features consistent with Owala's broader special-edition bottle lineup. Target has not yet published final retail pricing for the collection, though at least one confirmed listing shows a 16-fluid-ounce stainless steel Pikachu design available on Target's website. Given that Owala's existing special-edition FreeSip bottles at Target typically retail in the range of $25 to $30 depending on size and finish, industry watchers have said the new Pokemon collection is likely to fall within that same general pricing tier, though exact prices for each of the five designs had not been officially confirmed as of the collection's launch. Target typically publishes new product drops to its website around 3 a.m. Eastern time, though the retailer had not officially confirmed the exact release time for the Pokemon collection ahead of Wednesday's launch, according to retail coverage tracking the release. Target did tease the collaboration on its website in the days leading up to launch, confirming the collection was arriving Wednesday without detailing full pricing or size information for each design at that time. Ahead of the official release, photos purporting to show the bottles already stocked on store shelves at some Target locations began circulating online, including images shared to social media and community forums showing the Charizard and Kanto Starter Trio designs apparently pulled directly from shelves before the collection's confirmed launch date. One widely shared image showed a bagged Charizard bottle still bearing a printed "Remove Before Display" instruction, suggesting at least some Target locations had received and begun unpacking shipments of the collection ahead of schedule. The character lineup selected for the collaboration leans on some of Pokemon's most consistently popular and recognizable figures. Pikachu, the franchise's mascot, anchors the collection, while Charizard and Gengar represent two of the series' most enduringly popular non-mascot characters among longtime fans. The inclusion of Eevee and its evolved forms, along with the original three Kanto starter Pokemon, rounds out a lineup aimed at covering a broad cross-section of the franchise's decades-spanning fan base without requiring more niche or recent character selections. The collaboration's timing is no coincidence. Wednesday's release coincides directly with Pokemon's 30th anniversary, marking three decades since Nintendo's original Pokemon video games first launched and sparked what has since grown into one of the best-selling media franchises in history, spanning video games, a long-running animated series, and a global trading card game. The Owala collaboration joins a broader wave of 30th-anniversary merchandise tied to the milestone, including a Pokemon Trading Card Game 30th Celebration set that has also drawn significant attention from collectors and retailers in recent weeks, as well as a separate collaboration between apparel brand Adidas and Pokemon featuring three bomber jackets sold exclusively through Dick's Sporting Goods. As with many of Owala's prior special-edition and licensed collaborations, the Pokemon collection is expected to be available for a limited time only, a pattern that has previously driven quick sellouts for the brand's other themed drops, including past Halloween-specific FreeSip designs and other limited-run collaborations sold exclusively through Target. Owala has built a reputation in recent years for regularly releasing themed and collaboration bottles through Target, a pattern that has turned each new drop into a closely watched event among the brand's dedicated fan following, many of whom track upcoming releases through retail-focused deal and collector community websites. The exact online release time and full pricing details for all five Pokemon designs are expected to become clear once Target's individual product listings go live, with retail tracking sites advising shoppers interested in the collection to check Target's website directly on the morning of the release, given the retailer's history of limited initial stock for similarly hyped licensed collaborations. Shoppers interested in the broader Owala lineup, including the brand's standard FreeSip water bottles in various sizes, can find those products available now through Target's website and in select stores, independent of the new Pokemon-specific collection's release. © Copyright 2026 IBTimes AU. title: Wizz Financial collaborates with City Union Bank to Unveil 'Wizz Voyager', the Ultimate Smart Travel Card
description: Wizz Financial collaborates with City Union Bank to Unveil 'Wizz Voyager', the Ultimate Smart Travel Card
content: MUMBAI, India , Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Marking a major milestone in cross-border financial integration, Wizz Financial's India business, Wizzmoni , and City Union Bank have partnered to launch Wizz Voyager —a next-generation, AI-powered travel card designed to transform how Indian residents navigate international foreign exchange. Built on Visa's global network, the solution addresses common travel hassles like hidden FX fees, exchange rate fluctuations, and multi-currency account management. Through this joint initiative, Indian travellers gain access to 37 international currencies on a single card, backed by real-time exchange locks and automated spending controls. Amir Nagammy, Founder & CEO of Wizz Financial , said: "This strategic partnership with City Union Bank represents a major step forward in uniting modern fintech capabilities with trusted traditional banking infrastructure. By aligning our global expertise with City Union Bank's strong institutional footprint, we are building a more connected financial ecosystem—one that expands opportunities for international travellers and reinforces our commitment to driving high-impact innovation across borders." CA Krishnan R, Director & CEO, Wizzmoni India, added: "Managing multiple currencies while travelling abroad historically meant dealing with fragmented tools, unpredictable forex margins, and operational friction. Wizz Voyager changes that paradigm completely. With support for 37 currencies—including 5 market exclusives—we are providing an all-in-one financial passport tailored specifically for the modern Indian student, professional, and global explorer." R. Vijay Anandh, MD & CEO, City Union Bank, stated: "As international travel grows, customers are looking for simpler and more convenient ways to manage their money overseas. Our partnership with Wizzmoni brings together our banking capabilities with Wizzmoni's expertise in foreign exchange and travel solutions. The co-branded City Union Bank–Wizz Voyager multi-currency travel card gives travellers greater flexibility in managing multiple currencies, while providing greater transparency and control over their spending abroad. We see this partnership as a step towards making international travel and cross-border payments more seamless for our customers." About Wizz Voyager Card Wizz Voyager is an AI-powered multi-currency prepaid travel card designed for global travelers, including students, professionals, and tourists. Supporting 37 currencies, it delivers a seamless digital forex experience through a feature-rich mobile app with real-time tracking and smart financial controls. Built on Wizz Financial's proprietary end-to-end issuing and processing platform, Wizz Voyager is among the few fintech offerings globally with complete control over card issuance and management. Issued in partnership with VISA, it combines global acceptance with next-generation agility, while supporting a wide range of currencies, including several that are rarely available in the Indian market. About Wizzmoni Wizzmoni Financial Services Ltd is an NBFC and AD-II licensed financial services provider with more than 360 branches across India, offering digital wallet solutions, multi-currency travel cards, foreign exchange, send money abroad services, Gold loan, digital payments, and insurance. Wizzmoni is a flagship brand of Wizz Financial. About Wizz Financial Wizz Financial is a neo-banking platform focused on cross-border money movement and lending across strategic economic corridors spanning India, the GCC, Southeast Asia and the United States. Combining digital infrastructure with physical service networks, the Group delivers financial services across multiple markets through a hybrid operating model. About City Union Bank City Union Bank Ltd., the oldest Private Sector Bank in India, was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu, India. The Bank has completed 120+ years of service to the nation. The Bank has ~1001 branches spread across the country. CUB has always been a pioneer in providing advanced technology solutions to meet the evolving needs of its diverse customer base. Tap, pay & go payments through Key chain and fitness watch, voice-based authentication for logging into Mobile banking, Multi-lingual Voice Chatbot in regional languages, Voice-based UPI123 pay, End-to-End digital loan processing and Nap ID fraud filter layer are the latest innovations in this direction. www.wizzfinancial.com | www.wizzmoni.com | 1800 102 0555 “This is a company press release that is not part of editorial content. No journalist of The Hindubusinessline was involved in the publication of this release.” Published on September 16, 2026

content: The transaction will see Genpact occupy the entire tower at Kings Canyon, one of the within ASF Insignia, an integrated commercial IT office campus spread over 50 acres in Gurgaon. “The transaction highlights the growing demand from large enterprises for Grade A, scalable and integrated office environments that combine workplace quality with operational efficiency,” said Aanchal Saraf Aggarwal, Director, ASF Group. The transaction also reflects the continued evolution of Gurugram's office market, with large enterprises increasingly seeking workplaces that can combine scale, flexibility, employee experience and long-term operational efficiency within a single campus. “India's office market has endured three major global shocks in the last 25 years — the outsourcing-era cost race, the 2008 financial crisis, and the pandemic-driven work-from-home experiment — and emerged stronger from each one. History shows that every disruption has pushed occupiers up the value chain, from cost arbitrage to consolidation to capability building. The record leasing and expansion intent we see in 2026 is simply proof that the office market's long-term structural story remains firmly intact. Shocks create hesitation; India creates conviction,” said Vibhor Jain, Founder & CEO, CG offices. Earlier, Smartworks had leased approximately 450,000 sq ft space in ASF Campus. ASF has already delivered over five million sq ft of workspaces. The campus offers bonded SEZ space, de-bonded SEZ space and commercial IT park facilities within a single integrated development. description:

In the first auction, the central bank received bids worth Rs 3,17,088 crore for a not…
content: RBI absorbs ₹2.9 trillion via two VRRR auctions amid surplus liquidity The RBI, since last month, has been conducting various VRRR auctions in order to absorb surplus liquidity from the banking system and align the overnight money market rates to the repo rate Listen to This Article The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday absorbed ₹2.90 trillion through two variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auctions from the banking system amid a huge surplus. In the first auction, the central bank received bids worth ₹3,17,088 crore for a notified amount of ₹2.50 trillion. However, it accepted only ₹2,50,025 crore at a cut-off and weighted average rate of 5.24 per cent. The central bank received a tepid response in the second auction with bids worth ₹40,302 crore for a notified amount of ₹1 trillion, which it accepted fully. The RBI, since last month, has been conducting various VRRR auctions in order to absorb surplus liquidity from the banking system and align the overnight money market rates to the repo rate. Currently, liquidity in the banking system is estimated to be in surplus of around ₹9.85 trillion as on September 15. Also Read Apart from VRRR, last week, the central bank announced Open Market Operation (OMO) sales of government securities for a notified amount of ₹1 trillion in three tranches, with the auction for the first tranche of ₹50,000 crore to be held on September 17. The auction for two remaining tranches of ₹25,000 crore each will be held on September 21 and September 28, RBI said. The banking system was flushed with liquidity due to heavy mobilisation of FCNR (B) deposits by banks, as the mobilisation brought foreign currency into the system, while subsequent swaps with the RBI provided rupee liquidity to banks. Besides FCNR(B) inflows, month-end government expenditure, including payments toward salaries and pensions, also added to liquidity in the banking system. title: Voyager 1 is over 15.8 billion miles from Earth and its generators lose about four watts of power every year
description: Launched in 1977 on a four-year mission to Jupiter and Saturn, Voyager 1 is now the most distant human-made object — and the plutonium batteries keeping it alive weaken by roughly four watts a year.
content: On 5 September 1977, a Titan IIIE/Centaur rocket lifted off from Cape Canaveral carrying Voyager 1 toward Jupiter and Saturn. NASA’s Voyager FAQ gives the spacecraft’s launch mass, including hydrazine, as 815 kilograms. Forty-nine years later, the probe is still transmitting from interstellar space. NASA’s current mission-status page says Voyager 1 will reach one light-day from Earth, 16,094,799,096 miles, on 18 November 2026. At that distance, radio signals need nearly a full day to travel one way between Earth and the spacecraft. A command-and-response cycle therefore stretches across almost two days. What an RTG actually is A radioisotope thermoelectric generator is not a fission reactor with control rods or a chain reaction. NASA’s Radioisotope Power Systems FAQ explains that an RTG converts heat from the natural radioactive decay of plutonium-238 into electricity through thermocouples and the Seebeck effect. Voyager uses the older Multi-Hundred Watt RTG, or MHW-RTG, design. NASA lists each Voyager MHW-RTG at 158 watts of electrical output at the beginning of the mission, giving three units a combined beginning-of-mission output of roughly 474 watts. The generators have no turbine, piston, or other moving power-conversion machinery, which is one reason they can work for decades. NASA’s Voyager spacecraft description confirms that three RTGs supply electrical power and that loads have to be switched off as their output declines. Why the power keeps falling The plutonium does not suddenly stop producing heat when it reaches some expiration date. Its radioactive decay produces a slow decline, while the spacecraft has less and less electrical power available to distribute among instruments, heaters, communications, and other systems. The operational number is remarkably small but relentless. NASA says each Voyager’s RTG puts out about four watts less electrical power every year. Four watts is trivial in a house, but it is significant on a spacecraft whose available power has already fallen to well under half its beginning-of-mission level. Every remaining load therefore competes for a shrinking electrical budget. Turning off the lights, one instrument at a time Voyager’s prime-mission science payload consisted of 10 instruments, representing 11 investigations when radio science is counted. Many were shut down after the planetary encounters, including the imaging system in 1990 after Voyager 1 completed its final family portrait of the solar system. The process has continued as the power margin has tightened. In NASA’s April 17, 2026 mission update, engineers shut down Voyager 1’s low-energy charged particle experiment, leaving the plasma wave subsystem and magnetometer as its two operating science instruments. Engineers have also looked for power outside the science instruments themselves. In 2023, NASA described a strategy that tapped a small reserve of RTG power previously held for a voltage-regulation safety circuit, allowing Voyager 2 to postpone another science-instrument shutdown. The conservation work is still evolving. In an August 2026 update, NASA said engineers had freed additional power on Voyager 2 through a group of changes nicknamed the “Big Bang,” and that the mission planned to perform the same swap on Voyager 1. The fuel supply problem back on Earth Plutonium-238 for space power systems has to be manufactured deliberately rather than mined as a ready-to-use fuel. Oak Ridge National Laboratory reported in 2015 that its process starts with neptunium-237, which is irradiated before the resulting plutonium is chemically separated and converted into oxide. That 2015 run produced 50 grams of Pu-238 and restored a U.S. production capability that had been dormant for nearly 30 years after production at the Savannah River Plant ended in the late 1980s. The milestone mattered because radioisotope-powered missions consume fuel on a kilogram scale, not a gram scale. For comparison, NASA says Perseverance’s Multi-Mission RTG uses 4.8 kilograms of plutonium dioxide as its heat source. That rover uses a newer RTG design, but the quantity shows why producing space-qualified radioisotope fuel is a substantial undertaking. What the record actually shows about the end Voyager 1 is not approaching a moment when its plutonium suddenly runs out. The practical limit arrives when the declining electrical output is no longer enough to operate the remaining spacecraft systems and science instruments. NASA has been careful not to give that moment a guaranteed date. In JPL’s 2025 power-conservation update, engineers said the two Voyagers could retain enough electricity for at least one science instrument into the 2030s, while warning that unexpected spacecraft problems could shorten that timeline. Whenever the final transmission comes, Voyager 1 will continue moving through the galaxy. NASA’s 2026 trajectory update says the probe is heading toward AC +79 3888, better known as Gliese 445, and should pass within about 1.7 light-years of the star in roughly 40,000 years. It will still carry the Golden Record, the gold-plated phonograph disc containing sounds, images, music, and greetings from Earth. Long after its transmitter falls silent, the spacecraft itself will keep going. Four watts a year sounds almost insignificant. For Voyager 1, that slow loss is now the unit by which engineers trade electrical power for a little more time in interstellar space.

title: STAR WARS Zero Company Review
description: A clone in the dark
content: Pros & Cons - - Excellent tactical combat - A fantastic ragtag crew - Well-told story - Plenty of emergent moments - - Combat can get repetitive - Technical issues - Linear exploration - Unbalanced progression There’s no escaping the obvious: Star Wars Zero Company is essentially XCOM 3 in a galaxy far, far away. Developed by Bit Reactor, a studio founded by former XCOM developers, the game wears its inspiration proudly. But thankfully, it isn’t simply a Star Wars skin slapped onto a familiar formula. At its best, Zero Company understands exactly what makes tactics RPGs compelling and uses the Star Wars universe to further bolster that familiar genre formula. Set during the final stages of the Clone Wars, the game follows your custom character named Hawks (first name Rebecca in my case), a former Republic captain who now leads a small group of mercenaries. Her crew is exactly the kind of mismatched ensemble you’d expect from Star Wars: clones, smugglers, bounty hunters, former Separatists, Jedi and other assorted weirdos thrown together by circumstance. The overarching story, involving a mysterious cult known as the Coil, is not the most surprising story, but it is an incredibly well-told one. Where the narrative really succeeds is in the smaller, character-driven stories between the big beats. The relationship between the members of Zero Company is the emotional core of the game. Spending time with the crew, learning their histories and watching relationships evolve makes returning to the base almost as important as heading into battle. Characters can form bonds that affect their abilities, giving the familiar "found family" trope a meaningful mechanical purpose. It also makes permadeath sting considerably more when a character you’ve invested in disappears from the story for good (though I was a coward and turned permadeath off immediately). And then there’s the combat, which is easily the strongest part of the package. Every character gets three action points per turn, with positioning, cover, abilities and teamwork determining how effectively you can use them. The basic structure will be immediately familiar to anyone who has played modern XCOM, but Zero Company adds enough Star Wars flavour to keep things interesting. Jedi fight with lightsabers and Force abilities, Mandalorians can use jetpacks, droids bring their own utility, and different character specialisations encourage experimentation with squad compositions. The best missions go beyond simply eliminating every enemy. Objectives can involve evacuations, timed escapes, civilians, multiple enemy factions or constantly changing battlefield conditions. These scenarios create the kind of emergent moments tactical games thrive on: carefully setting up an overwatch trap, pulling off a last-second rescue or watching a plan collapse because one crucial shot missed. Unfortunately, the game doesn't maintain that freshness throughout its entire runtime. The campaign runs roughly 30–40 hours, and both the combat encounters and character interactions can become less varied as you progress. Resource management also creates interesting decisions, but the economy can feel restrictive, forcing you to choose between competing upgrades rather than letting you meaningfully develop every system. The bigger problem is technical. Camera issues, clipping, framerate drops, long pauses during combat and occasional freezes can interrupt otherwise excellent battles. Though I personally found them more charming than irritating, because a lot of these issues are ones carried right over from XCOM. It feels less like a flaw and more like an author’s signature. Bit Reactor have brought over that bad habits along with the good ones. The third-person exploration sections are also an odd fit; they look great and help sell the scale of the Star Wars world, but often feel unnecessary compared with the tactical missions, especially since the levels are entirely linear. If you’re expecting exploration on the level of, say, Marvel’s Midnight Suns, you might be disappointed. Still, when everything clicks, Star Wars Zero Company delivers exactly the kind of Star Wars experience fans have been asking for: a character-driven story, a memorable ragtag crew and genuinely satisfying battles. It may not reinvent the XCOM formula, but it proves that the formula works remarkably well in this universe. Zero Company isn't a flawless game, and its technical roughness prevents it from reaching its full potential. But beneath the jank is a smart, addictive tactical RPG with enough personality to stand on its own. For Star Wars fans who also enjoy XCOM-style strategy, there's plenty here to sink your teeth into. Final Thoughts STAR WARS Zero Company Review Zero Company doesn't reinvent tactical RPGs but the combination of excellent combat, a lovable crew and an uniquely authentic Star Wars story makes this an easy recommendation for fans of both. It carries over some of XCOM's rougher edges along with its best ideas, but when it comes together, it really sings.

title: US limits visas for South African officials over alleged anti-white discrimination
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says South Africa has not addressed US concerns over racial inequality.
content: - Published The US has announced visa restrictions targeting people it accuses of discriminating against South Africa's white minority, in the latest escalation of tensions between the two countries. The Trump administration has criticised South Africa over several issues, including policies aimed at addressing racial inequality that it says discriminate against Afrikaners, descendants mainly of Dutch and French settlers. South Africa has repeatedly denied the claim. South Africa's Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola said he noted the announcement with "concern". "The announcement once again, [sic] aligns with the mischaracterisation of South Africa's domestic policies by fringe groups who wrongly portray themselves as representatives of 'minorities' and Afrikaners in general," said a statement from the international relations and co-operation ministry. Announcing the restrictions on Tuesday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: "The South African government has not adequately addressed the previously laid out concerns." He said the visa restrictions would target those who promote "race-based discrimination, incite violence, or enable land confiscation without compensation in South Africa." Rubio did not immediately name any individuals targeted by the restrictions. Relations between the two countries have been on a downward spiral since President Donald Trump returned to office early last year, with the US leader cutting aid, expelling the South African ambassador and offering "refuge" to white South Africans fleeing "persecution." The South African government has repeatedly rejected allegations that it is persecuting white people or confiscating their land. South Africa's latest crime statistics do not indicate that white people are at a greater risk of violent crime than other racial groups. Trump offered refugee status to Afrikaners last year after South African President Cyril Ramaphosa signed a law allowing the government to seize land without compensation in rare instances. The legislation allows the state to expropriate property in the public interest and provides for circumstances in which compensation may be set at zero. But it also requires authorities, in most cases, to first try to reach an agreement with property owners, and disputes can be taken to court. Land ownership remains a highly sensitive issue in South Africa more than three decades after the end of apartheid, under which the black majority was dispossessed of land and denied many basic rights. The government says land reform is necessary to address those historic inequalities and insists the new law does not permit arbitrary seizures. Most private farmland is owned by white South Africans, who make up just over 7% of the population. In Wednesday's statement, South Africa's government said: "It is our sovereign right to put in place laws that address the nation's concern over centuries of racial injustice." In a separate social media post on Tuesday, Rubio accused South Africa's government of pursuing "racial grievance against the Afrikaner minority" and said those responsible for what he described as injustices "have no place in the United States". He said the South African government had failed to adequately address US concerns about what Washington describes as "government-sponsored discrimination" against Afrikaners and other minorities. "The United States will not allow such behaviour to go unchecked," he added. He said the actions targeted by the policy undermined "peace, economic stability and the rule of law." The US embassy in Pretoria said Washington believed dialogue with South Africa had run its course and accused the African country of failing to demonstrate a commitment to strong bilateral relations. It warned that the new visa restrictions were the beginning of tougher measures, adding: "This visa restriction policy is only the first step in a series of escalatory measures that will show America's firm resolve in this matter." South Africa made efforts to soothe tensions with US, with Ramaphosa going to the White House in May last year with a large delegation that included white members of his coalition government and also famous white South African golfers. But Trump ambushed the Oval Office meeting with claims that white South African farmers were being killed and "persecuted" - producing unsubstantiated evidence that has been widely discredited. Further efforts by South Africa to mend the relationship have failed, with Africa's largest economy being hit in August with 30% tariffs on goods being exported to the US - the highest rate in sub-Saharan Africa. The latest visa restrictions are being imposed under a provision of US immigration law that allows the secretary of state to bar foreign nationals whose entry is considered potentially damaging to US foreign policy interests.

title: How long will birds sit on unfertilized eggs?
description: How Long Will Birds Sit on Unfertilized Eggs?: Understanding Incubation Instincts A bird’s dedication to incubation is powerful, but even the strongest instinct has its limits. Generally, most birds will abandon an unfertilized egg after the typical incubatio…
content: A bird’s dedication to incubation is powerful, but even the strongest instinct has its limits. Generally, most birds will abandon an unfertilized egg after the typical incubation period has passed or shortly thereafter, ranging from a few days to a couple of weeks depending on the species. Incubation is a crucial and fascinating aspect of avian reproduction. It involves consistent warmth and protection provided by the parent bird to develop embryos within eggs. However, what happens when an egg is not fertilized? How long will birds sit on unfertilized eggs? The answer to this question depends on several factors, including the bird species, the strength of the incubation instinct, and environmental cues. The incubation instinct is a deeply ingrained behavior driven by hormones and triggered by the presence of eggs in a nest. This instinct compels birds to: - Maintain a specific nest temperature - Turn eggs regularly for even development - Protect the nest from predators - Even brood eggs that are not theirs This powerful drive ensures the survival of the next generation. The intensity and duration of this instinct vary significantly between species and even individual birds. While birds may possess impressive instincts, they cannot visually determine if an egg is fertilized early in the incubation process. Some birds may be able to detect differences in weight or subtle changes within the egg through careful observation, but the determination of fertilization status takes time. How long will birds sit on unfertilized eggs? The answer depends heavily on the typical incubation period for that particular bird species. Birds typically incubate eggs until they hatch. After the normal incubation period is over, birds will remain vigilant, giving the eggs some additional time to hatch. After that period has passed, the bird will usually give up on the eggs and start nesting elsewhere, or focus their attention on food. External factors also influence incubation behavior. For example: - Food Availability: If food becomes scarce, a bird might abandon unfertilized eggs sooner to prioritize its own survival. - Predator Pressure: Constant threats can disrupt incubation and lead to nest abandonment. - Weather Conditions: Extreme weather can endanger both the parent bird and the eggs, potentially shortening the incubation period. Several factors can result in unfertilized eggs: - Inexperienced Mates: Young birds might not be successful at mating. - Infertility: Older birds or those with health problems may have reduced fertility. - Mating Problems: Physical incompatibilities or behavioral issues can prevent successful fertilization. - Environmental Factors: Pollution or toxins can affect fertility. While the instinct to incubate is strong, prolonged incubation of unfertilized eggs can have negative consequences: - Energy Depletion: The bird expends valuable energy on a futile effort, potentially weakening its overall health. - Missed Breeding Opportunities: Prolonged incubation can delay or prevent a second breeding attempt in the same season. - Increased Risk of Predation: Spending excessive time at the nest increases the risk of the parent bird being attacked. How can I tell if an egg is unfertilized without disturbing the nest? It’s difficult to know for sure without candling (shining a bright light through the egg), which is best left to experienced bird handlers to avoid disturbance. However, if the typical incubation period has passed and there’s still no sign of hatching, it’s a strong indication the egg is unfertilized. Observe from a distance to avoid disturbing the bird further. What should I do if I find a nest with abandoned unfertilized eggs? In most cases, it’s best to leave the nest undisturbed. Nature will take its course. Removing the eggs could encourage the birds to rebuild a new nest, leading to more energy expenditure. However, if the nest poses a hazard, consult with a local wildlife rehabilitation center. Does replacing unfertilized eggs with fertile ones help the situation? Generally, it is not recommended to interfere with a bird’s nest by replacing eggs. This can disrupt the natural process and potentially introduce diseases or behavioral problems. Furthermore, moving eggs is illegal in many places. Will a bird lay more eggs if its first clutch is unfertilized? Yes, many bird species will lay a second or even third clutch if their first nesting attempt fails. This is especially common in migratory birds with short breeding seasons. This depends on food supply and weather conditions, however. What is “candling” and how is it used to determine egg fertility? Candling involves shining a bright light through an eggshell in a darkened room. A fertilized egg will typically show visible veins and a developing embryo. An unfertilized egg will appear clear or uniformly colored without signs of development. This is a delicate process best performed by experienced individuals. Are some bird species more prone to laying unfertilized eggs than others? Yes, factors like age, health, and genetic compatibility can influence fertility. Some species may also be more susceptible to environmental toxins that affect reproductive success. Do male birds play a role in determining egg fertility? Yes, the male bird’s fertility is just as important as the female’s. Infertile males will naturally result in unfertilized eggs. How does diet affect a bird’s ability to lay fertilized eggs? A proper diet rich in calcium, protein, and vitamins is essential for egg production and fertility. Nutritional deficiencies can lead to weaker eggs or reduced fertility. What happens to the unfertilized eggs after the bird abandons the nest? In most cases, the eggs will decompose naturally. Scavengers may also consume them. Over time, the eggshells will break down and become part of the environment. Is it possible for an egg to appear fertile but still not hatch? Yes, there are instances of early embryonic death. The egg might appear to be developing initially, but for various reasons, the embryo stops growing before hatching. Can environmental pollutants affect egg fertility? Absolutely. Exposure to pesticides, heavy metals, and other pollutants can negatively impact a bird’s reproductive system and reduce egg fertility. It’s vital to protect habitats from pollution to ensure healthy bird populations. Does the age of a bird influence the likelihood of unfertilized eggs? Yes, very young or very old birds are more likely to lay unfertilized eggs or eggs with thin shells. Prime breeding age typically corresponds with optimal fertility.

title: L'Oreal steals French stock market crown from LVMH
description: Cosmetics group L'Oreal became France's most valuable listed company yesterday, surpassing Louis Vuitton owner LVMH as high-end luxury companies remain under ⁠pressure after years of slowing sales and lacklustre earnings.
content: Cosmetics group L'Oreal became France's most valuable listed company yesterday, surpassing Louis Vuitton owner LVMH as high-end luxury companies remain under pressure after years of slowing sales and lacklustre earnings. It is the first time since 2017 that a non-luxury company has claimed the top spot on the Paris bourse at the end of a trading day. Berenberg analyst Nick Anderson pointed to the lipstick effect - when the economic mood is bleak, it becomes easier to sell small treats rather than high-end handbags, shoes and dresses. "People simply can't afford to buy these expensive luxury items and instead are indulging in small luxuries like the proverbial lipstick to make themselves feel better," he said. L'Oreal's market capitalisation reached around €203 billion yesterday evening, according to LSEG data, with LVMH at €201 billion. Hit by a prolonged economic slump in China and the war in the Middle East, the global luxury industry has been contracting over the last three years. According to consultancy Bain, around 60 million consumers have turned their backs on luxury goods as persistent price hikes have pushed high-end fashion brands out of reach for many buyers. Shares in L'Oreal, which also produces high-end cosmetics for fashion labels like Armani and Yves Saint Laurent, are up 5% this year, compared with a year-to-date loss of 35% for LVMH. LVMH, controlled by the family of CEO Bernard Arnault, became Europe's most valuable company amid a pandemic-era spending boom in 2021, but today is dwarfed by chipmaker ASML - now worth three times as much - and Swiss pharmaceutical giants Roche and Novartis. Its shares were down 2.3% yesterday. Based on current stock market data, LVMH yesterday also lost its place among Europe's 10 largest companies by market capitalisation. Arnault, meanwhile, has lost his title as Europe's wealthiest person to Zara founder Amancio Ortega, according to Forbes' real-time billionaire ranking. Apart from a resilient but small group of ultra-rich shoppers, LVMH is suffering from a structural lack of demand, Anderson said, pointing to the economic downturn in China, once the industry's growth engine, and other factors. "We're scared about tax rises everywhere across Europe. You've got inflation worries, you've got AI job worries. There's just something everywhere," Anderson said. "I don't see luxury trends significantly improving," DWS equity portfolio manager Stefan Bauknecht said, adding that L'Oreal's new lead could well be here to stay.

title: Eating grass, meditation and more – What Tuchel said in viral documentary
description: The FA have released a documentary called Reflections: England's World Cup Journey; Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel looks back on the summer campaign and explains how it has bonded him and the group for the upcoming Nations League and Euro 2028 challenges
content: Thomas Tuchel: England boss on World Cup reflections, wishing he'd eaten Azteca grass and an 'exciting' future The FA have released a documentary called Reflections: England's World Cup Journey; Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel looks back on the summer campaign and explains how it has bonded him and the group for the upcoming Nations League and Euro 2028 challenges Wednesday 16 September 2026 09:20, UK Thomas Tuchel wishes he'd eaten grass from the Azteca pitch after England's World Cup win over Mexico this summer. That's just one of the statements from the England boss which has drawn attention across social media, following the FA releasing a new documentary called 'Reflections: England's World Cup Journey'. In the documentary, Tuchel sits alongside former England international and Sky Sports pundit Daniel Sturridge to look back on England's campaign, which ultimately saw the team finish third, having lost in the semi-finals to Argentina. England's standout performance of the tournament came in the last-16 win over Mexico in Mexico City, where they played for over 35 minutes with 10 men but prevailed 3-2. "I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, 'I regret that I didn't eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever'," said Tuchel. On the unity his players showed in that match, Tuchel pointed to their reaction to Jordan Henderson falling and breaking his arm in the post-match celebrations. "If you needed any proof, any proof for what it meant to these players and how they were with each other, it was the moment when Jordan fell over and broke his arm," said Tuchel. "Within a second, the players were there, every single player was there, stopping the celebrations, building a shield, protecting Jordan and not going nowhere in full empathy. It was just so special." The film will be released on Wednesday September 16 exclusively on the England app. The build-up to the Mexico game had been dominated by talk of the altitude of the Azteca stadium but also the potential for weather delays, which proved founded with kick-off pushed back. But Tuchel says a calm came over the group when they trained together in Mexico before the match and meditation and manifestation helped them to achieve the victory. "In the middle of Mexico City and we arrived and it's an oasis, it's so peaceful, it's an unbelievable pitch and it is so calm, it is so peaceful that it did something to the players," said Tuchel. "They came out from the gym straight out on the pitch, they were having phone calls, walking around, it was such a peaceful energy. "So we came up with this line of 'silence is powerful', that we enjoy the silence, we're in a home country, we will play against the whole nation, the whole nation will be against us, the stadium, it's almost impossible to win in the stadium, no one has ever done it before in a World Cup match. "So let's enjoy the silence, the power of the silence. We even had five minutes on the match day of meditation and manifestation of the last whistle." The FA are currently undergoing a review of England's World Cup campaign but Tuchel says the experience has bonded him and the group together and he is "excited" about what comes next. England face world champions Spain in the Nations League in the upcoming international break with the 2028 Euros the next major tournament. Tuchel reckons preparing for that tournament will be easier than the planning which was required for the 2026 World Cup. "It created a huge bond to these players, it feels like they are my players now. This is the beauty of it," said Tuchel. "When you have a manager and then you have success and you have painful moments together, but you have so much time together and then you create a natural bond. "I'm happy to see them, I'm happy to challenge them, happy to push them and very proud to be a part of them. "I'm very excited. I'm excited to work with these players. I'm excited to have new, young players that we can bring into camp and that they can learn. "We've got another step closer and I think we're there. "It's very difficult to prepare a World Cup in the US, but it's possible to prepare for a Euros and be prepared in Nations League tier one. "The target is to have another 10 matches. We had 10 matches in the US, eight wins, one draw, one painful loss, but that is something to build on. "We have all the right to hold our heads high and go with courage and positivity into the next challenges. "We have four matches in the Nations League coming up and that's where the focus is." Tuchel on Harry Kane going to another level "Just so easy. He's always there, he's always in training, he always wants to train. The level to which he got himself now, since he's at Bayern Munich. "The level of commitment and training, how he arrived in prep camp, how he arrived in the qualification matches, the speech after the October camp, and he straight away stood up in the dressing room and said, 'guys, we will keep on going in November, this is what we do'. "He found another level in his game, but also as a personality, and how he shows up for training, how he drives training standards is one of a kind. The finishing is out of control good." On Jude Bellingham living up to his full potential "He was one of the players of the tournament, not only for us, but of the whole tournament. "He lived up to his full potential, you could just see what a competitor, what a machine he is, and he just thrives on the pressure. He just loves these moments, he loves these stages, it brings out the very best. "He came with an amazing mindset into camp, with the best physical preparation. He came fresh, he came hungry, hungry for football, hungry for minutes into camp. He took his place and decided every single match for us." On the England fans and their 'special' connection with the team "They lived up to the high expectations. "Everyone told me, 'wait until the tournament starts, we will have the best fans, we will be right on top, it will be amazing, the amount of people…' and it was just like that from the first moment. "They just felt this team. I believe that fans have a sense, maybe they cannot name it, someone will say, 'yeah, they give everything, they're sweating, after the whistle goes, they have to sit down because they're so tired'. For everyone it's maybe different, they feel it, they could sense it, that this team is together and this team means it. "That's what made the connection so strong. That was not artificial. That was very special."

title: Why is it illegal to collect bird feathers in the US?
description: Why Is It Illegal to Collect Bird Feathers in the US? The act of collecting bird feathers in the US is largely illegal due to federal laws, primarily the Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA), designed to protect bird populations and prevent their exploitation. Th…
content: The act of collecting bird feathers in the US is largely illegal due to federal laws, primarily the Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA), designed to protect bird populations and prevent their exploitation. These laws make it unlawful to possess, buy, sell, or barter migratory bird parts, including feathers. The reasons behind the prohibition on collecting bird feathers are rooted in a dark chapter of conservation history. In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, the millinery trade – the fashion industry centered on hats – fueled the massacre of countless birds. Plumes, especially those of egrets, herons, and other showy species, were highly prized for adorning fashionable hats. This demand nearly drove some species to extinction. The dire situation prompted action. Concerned citizens and early conservationists lobbied for legislation to protect birds from overexploitation. This effort culminated in the Migratory Bird Treaty Act of 1918 (MBTA), a landmark law that remains the cornerstone of bird protection in the United States. The MBTA, initially enacted to protect birds migrating between the US, Canada, and Mexico (later expanded to include other countries), makes it illegal to “pursue, hunt, take, capture, kill, attempt to take, capture or kill, possess, offer for sale, sell, offer to barter, barter, offer to purchase, purchase, deliver for shipment, ship, export, import, cause to be shipped, exported, or imported, receive for shipment, export, or import, in any manner any migratory bird, any part, nest, or egg of any such bird…” without a permit. This sweeping language encompasses a broad range of activities, including simply possessing a feather found on the ground. The strict enforcement of the MBTA, even for seemingly harmless activities like collecting fallen feathers, is crucial for several reasons: - Preventing Exploitation: It discourages the commercial exploitation of birds and their parts. Even small-scale collection could create a market that incentivizes illegal hunting and trapping. - Enforcement Clarity: A blanket prohibition simplifies enforcement. Allowing collection of some feathers would create loopholes and difficulties in distinguishing legally obtained feathers from illegally obtained ones. - Protecting Vulnerable Species: Some bird populations remain vulnerable, and any additional pressure, even seemingly minor, could hinder their recovery. - Ecosystem Health: Birds play vital roles in ecosystems, including pollination, seed dispersal, and pest control. Protecting birds contributes to overall environmental health. While a general prohibition exists, there are exceptions to the MBTA for certain activities: - Native American Religious Purposes: The Eagle Feather Law allows Native Americans to possess eagle feathers and other bird parts for religious and cultural purposes. However, strict regulations apply. - Scientific and Educational Purposes: Permits can be obtained for scientific research, educational displays, and other activities that contribute to bird conservation. - Taxidermy and Salvage: Permits may be issued for taxidermy and salvage of bird specimens under specific circumstances. The following table summarizes the key aspects of legal and illegal feather collection in the US: Many people misunderstand the intricacies of bird feather protection laws. Common misconceptions include: - “It’s okay to collect feathers if the bird is dead.” The MBTA prohibits possession of any migratory bird part, regardless of how the bird died. - “It’s only illegal to sell feathers, not to collect them.” Possession alone is illegal without a permit. - “This law is outdated and unnecessary.” Bird populations still face numerous threats, and the MBTA remains a vital tool for their protection. The MBTA has been subject to legal challenges and proposed revisions in recent years. Some have argued for a more limited interpretation of the law, focusing on intentional harm to birds rather than incidental take. Others advocate for strengthening the MBTA to address emerging threats like habitat loss and climate change. The future of bird protection laws in the US remains a dynamic and evolving area. Understanding why is it illegal to collect bird feathers in the US is crucial for responsible engagement with nature and supporting bird conservation efforts. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Why is it illegal to collect bird feathers in the US, even if they’re just lying on the ground? The Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA) makes it illegal to possess migratory bird parts, including feathers, without a permit. This broad prohibition is in place to prevent the commercial exploitation of birds and to simplify enforcement, as distinguishing between legally and illegally obtained feathers would be difficult. Does this law apply to all types of bird feathers? The MBTA primarily covers migratory birds, which include most bird species found in the United States. However, some introduced, non-native species (like pigeons and starlings, in some jurisdictions) may be exempt. Always check with local authorities before collecting any feathers, and err on the side of caution. Are there any exceptions to the prohibition on collecting bird feathers? Yes, there are exceptions for Native American religious purposes (under the Eagle Feather Law), scientific research, and educational displays, all requiring permits. Can I get a permit to legally collect bird feathers? Permits for collecting bird feathers are rarely granted to private individuals. They are typically reserved for scientific, educational, or Native American religious purposes. What happens if I’m caught with illegal bird feathers? Penalties for violating the MBTA can include fines, seizure of the feathers, and even imprisonment, depending on the severity of the offense. What should I do if I find a bird feather that I want to identify or study? Instead of collecting the feather, consider taking a photograph of it and using online resources or field guides to identify the bird species it came from. You can also report the finding to a local wildlife organization. Does the law apply to feathers found in my own backyard? Yes, the MBTA applies regardless of where the feather is found, including your private property. If a non-native bird species (like a pigeon) drops a feather, is it legal to collect it? The legality of collecting feathers from non-native species can vary depending on state and local laws. It’s best to check with your local wildlife agency to be sure. Does the MBTA protect all bird species, even those that are not endangered? Yes, the MBTA provides broad protection to most migratory bird species, regardless of their conservation status. The intention is to prevent future endangerment. Is it legal to buy or sell bird feathers online? No, it is illegal to buy or sell migratory bird feathers online (or anywhere else) without the appropriate permits. Online marketplaces actively remove listings that violate the MBTA. What is the purpose of the Eagle Feather Law? The Eagle Feather Law allows federally recognized Native American tribes to possess and use eagle feathers and other bird parts for religious and cultural ceremonies. It recognizes the deep cultural significance of these items to Native American traditions. How can I help protect birds in my community? You can support bird conservation by creating bird-friendly habitats in your yard, reducing your use of pesticides, avoiding single-use plastics, and supporting organizations dedicated to bird conservation. Educating yourself and others about bird protection laws is also essential. Why is it illegal to collect bird feathers in the US is just one small piece of the larger conservation puzzle.
