title: India placed better in economy despite global challenges, says FM Sitharaman
description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said India is better placed economically despite global challenges, citing tax reforms aimed at reducing litigation and simplifying compliance. Speaking at ITRAF’s Bengaluru conference, she urged industry and tax profession…
content: Listen to this article in summarized format Speaking at the International Tax Research and Analysis Foundation’s (ITRAF) 8th International Tax Conference in Bengaluru, Sitharaman said India was better placed economically despite challenges around the world and called for a more mature, evidence-based tax policy debate focused on the national interest. Also read: FM Sitharamran says AI researcher's resignation raises questions over safeguards “So, I wish to hear a submission that says, ‘here is a provision that no longer serves the tax system and ought to be removed even though we presently benefit from it’,” she said. She urged tax professionals, industry representatives and policy researchers to submit quantified alternatives that explain the impact of proposed changes on revenue, administration, compliance costs and other taxpayers, rather than making representations based solely on sectoral interests. Viksit Bharat 2047. Easier compliance, fewer tax disputes Sitharaman said the Centre’s tax reforms had focused on reducing litigation at its source rather than simply managing pending disputes. She cited the Vivad se Vishwas schemes, which gave taxpayers and the government an opportunity to settle longstanding disputes, and the increase in 2024 of the monetary thresholds for departmental appeals. The limits were raised to Rs 60 lakh before the appellate tribunal, Rs 2 crore before high courts and Rs 5 crore before the Supreme Court. Sitharaman also pointed to the reduction of the corporate tax rate to 22% in 2019 and the rationalisation of individual income tax rates in 2025, under which an individual with an income of Rs 12 lakh pays no income tax. The replacement of the Income Tax Act, 1961, with a shorter, plain-language code drafted in six months was another reform she cited. The new code was prepared without changing the overall tax burden. She said the consolidation of GST into essentially two primary rates in 2025 was also intended to reduce litigation by limiting disputes over the classification of goods and services. The government had additionally rationalised tax deducted at source and tax collected at source provisions, while reducing unnecessary criminal consequences under tax laws, she said. Also read: India's UPI MDR shake-up: What changes and why it matters FM seeks independent tax policy research Sitharaman said pre-budget submissions from institutions routinely narrowed down to requests for lower rates, exemptions or concessions. She called for representations that examined the wider consequences of proposed reforms, including their impact on the tax base, administration and other taxpayers. “If a provision is said to impose an excessive compliance burden, tell us how many taxpayers it affects, how much time or cost it imposes, and what an alternative would mean for revenue,” she said. “If a change is proposed, show us not only who gains from it but also its consequences for the tax base itself, administration and other taxpayers,” she added. The Finance Minister also urged professionals to identify potential unintended consequences of proposed changes and place the broader national interest ahead of sectoral considerations. On international taxation, Sitharaman recalled India’s renegotiation of tax treaties with Mauritius, Singapore and Cyprus to restore its right to tax capital gains at source. She also cited the implementation of General Anti-Avoidance Rules, the Multilateral Instrument and the expansion of the Advance Pricing Agreement programme, alongside new safe harbour provisions. Sitharaman called on ITRAF to move from quiet commentary to visible, independent research that could contribute to public policy discussions. She referred to institutions such as the UK's Institute for Fiscal Studies and the Netherlands-based IBFD as examples of research bodies that examine policy choices in depth. Independent tax research, she said, should become part of public discourse and help inform the choices shaping India’s economic future. (With inputs from agencies)

title: A teenager who survived childhood cancer started collecting LEGO for the hospital that treated him; his drive has now donated 573 mini-figures and raised $2,575
description: Cancer survivor Alexander Ackles-Dold reminisces about the compassion he received during his childhood hospital stays. In a heartfelt initiative, he spearheads a LEGO donation drive for the pediatric oncology clinic in Southlake. The project has amassed hundr…
content: Sometimes a small act of kindness goes so far that it touches your heart for an entire lifetime. Alexander Ackled-Dold still remembers the little things when he was receiving treatment for leukaemia as a child at Southlake's pediatric oncology clinic. The teen recounted how the staff were always kind as he was in and out of hospitals for treatment, they drew smiley faces on his bandages and one volunteer even provided LEGO minifigures to the children whenever they came in for treatment. Now in Grade 12 and cancer-free, he said those actions have made a lifetime of difference and inspired him to do the same for others going through treatment today. “Whenever I would go, I just remembered the little things some of the nurses would do that would make the visit less about me going there to get a treatment,” he said. Thus, Alexander and his family launched the Southlake Superheroes donation drive in September. The campaign sought donations of LEGO figures and cash to donate to Southlake's pediatric oncology clinic. So far, the initiative has donated 573 mini-figures and raised more than $2,575 to help provide new LEGO sets. His father, Simon Ackles-Dold, said the initiative has gone well so far, with the children loving the little figures by all counts. "There was good initial feedback, positive feedback," he said. “A lot of the younger kids at Alex’s school were donating their old LEGO figures, so lots of teenagers were giving, which is really nice to see.” The project aims to give kids something fun to look forward to when they receive treatment, akin to what Alexander experienced when he was younger and in that situation. “It’s a good distraction for the kids when they’re there,” Ackles-Dold said. While the campaign does not donate to the children directly, since access is limited during treatment, Alexander said it was great interacting with staff there again, years after he was a patient. “It’s been a long time, and it’s been nice to give back to them and see them all happy about what I’m doing,” he said. The family hopes to be able to grow the effort and continue fundraising in the coming months. They are still collecting cash donations or donations of LEGO figures, though old LEGO sets are disallowed because of the need to sterilise whatever they donate. Interested individuals can donate by contacting the Southlake Heroes Instagram page or GoFundMe page, helping the family continue a simple tradition of kindness that once meant so much to Alexander himself.

title: Global Industry-Academia-Government Dialogue on Future of CO2 Utilization: 8th International Conference on Carbon Recycling 2026 to Be Held on October 9 at The Westin Tokyo
description: -Hybrid Conference Bringing Together Government, Industry and Academic Leaders from Japan and Overseas- TOKYO, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Secretariat of International Conference on Carbon Recycling 2026 announced that the Ministry of Economy, Trade an…
content: -Hybrid Conference Bringing Together Government, Industry and Academic Leaders from Japan and Overseas- TOKYO, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Secretariat of International Conference on Carbon Recycling 2026 announced that the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) will hold the 8th International Conference on Carbon Recycling 2026 on Friday, October 9, 2026, at The Westin Tokyo. The conference serves as an international platform for sharing and discussing the latest R&D results and business cases in carbon recycling among industry, academia and government in Japan and around the world. Main image: https://cdn.kyodonewsprwire.jp/prwfile/release/M109200/202609045320/_prw_PI1fl_ueQ17u0Q.jpg 2025 conference photos: https://cdn.kyodonewsprwire.jp/prwfile/release/M109200/202609045320/_prw_PI2fl_9l6upv6F.jpg Held annually since its first edition in 2019, the conference brings together government officials, leading researchers and industry leaders to exchange knowledge about carbon recycling, including technology development, business deployment and international cooperation. As responding to climate change becomes increasingly urgent, carbon recycling, which treats emitted CO2 as a reusable resource, is considered as a key technology for achieving carbon neutrality and promoting the green transformation (GX). The upcoming International Conference on Carbon Recycling will be held in a hybrid format, both in-person and online, and the organizers are expecting many overseas government officials, researchers and companies to participate. Conference Outline -Date/Time: Friday, October 9, 2026; 13:00-17:30 JST -Venue: The Westin Tokyo (1-4-1 Mita, Meguro-ku, Tokyo 153-8580, Japan) -Format: Hybrid (in-person and online) -Languages: English/Japanese (simultaneous interpretation) -Participation fee: Free (advance registration required) -Organizers: METI and NEDO -Official website/registration: https://carbon-recycling2026.nedo.go.jp/en/ Program Main Sessions -Opening Ceremony -Session A: The Global Landscape of Carbon Recycling and Japan's Initiatives -Special Session -Session B: Advanced Carbon Recycling Technologies for CO2 Value Chain Development -Session C: Industrial Collaboration and Market Development for Carbon Recycling Deployment -Closing Ceremony Concurrent Events -Poster Session -Networking Reception -Startup Event -CR Exchange of Views for Students About the International Conference on Carbon Recycling METI and NEDO have held the International Conference on Carbon Recycling in Japan annually since 2019 to share carbon-recycling initiatives from Japan with the world and to promote cooperation with industry, academia and government worldwide. title: Tencent Cloud Named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Managed Edge Services
description: SHENZHEN, China, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tencent Cloud, the cloud business of global technology company Tencent, today announced that it has been named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Managed Edge Services 2026 Vendor Assessment (doc #US5412…
content: SHENZHEN, China, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tencent Cloud, the cloud business of global technology company Tencent, today announced that it has been named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Managed Edge Services 2026 Vendor Assessment (doc #US54122426, September 2026). According to the IDC MarketScape, "EdgeOne natively converges intelligent acceleration, DDoS protection, web application firewall, bot management, edge compute, edge storage, edge AI inference, as well as web application and AI agent development and deployment capabilities through EdgeOne Makers. Delivered through a unified platform, these capabilities help customers reduce the integration and operational complexity associated with managing multiple products." Building Edge Infrastructure for AI-Native Applications and High-Performance Edge AI Services The IDC MarketScape notes, "Content delivery performance and network proximity—the traditional value propositions of managed edge—are now baseline expectations rather than differentiators. The competitive frontier has shifted to AI inference at the edge, where vendors are being evaluated on GPU availability, model deployment tooling, inference latency, and token cost efficiency versus centralized cloud AI services." To address this shift, Tencent Cloud EdgeOne is evolving its global infrastructure into an edge foundation for AI-native applications. It provides enterprises with edge acceleration, security protection, edge AI inference, and full-stack capabilities to develop and deploy web applications and AI agents. On the security front, Tencent Cloud is expanding EdgeOne's protection capabilities beyond traditional cyberattacks to include the identification and management of emerging access patterns, including AI crawlers and AI agents. Tencent Cloud EdgeOne is bringing AI inference closer to end users to meet the real-time demands of modern applications. In scenarios such as real-time conversations, transactions, gaming interactions, and media content generation, response time directly affects user experience. Tencent Cloud EdgeOne's edge AI inference platform, Booster, extends the platform's globally distributed infrastructure from content delivery to AI computing. By deploying inference services closer to business applications, Booster enables image and video generation, voice and audio processing, storage, and caching to take place nearer to end users. This allows applications such as artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) production, real-time media processing, intelligent recommendations, and advertising decision-making to access computing resources closer to where they are needed, enabling millisecond-level response times. In the managed hosting sector, the rise of "vibe coding"—the practice of using AI to build applications through natural language—is expanding application development beyond websites toward the creation of AI agents. As large numbers of newly generated agents move into production environments, businesses are placing greater demands on rapid deployment and managed hosting. Tencent Cloud EdgeOne's edge hosting platform, Makers, now supports both web applications and AI agents in addition to traditional website hosting. Developers can bring completed projects online with minimal adaptation, without building and maintaining the underlying runtime infrastructure. Makers currently serves more than 500,000 users and hosts more than one million websites, supporting corporate websites, cross-border e-commerce, AI SaaS applications, and agents across various industries, including healthcare, government, and legal services. Edge AI Powers Real-Time Applications Across Gaming, Audio & Video, and E-Commerce Today, Tencent Cloud EdgeOne operates more than 3,200 edge nodes with over 400Tbps of network capacity and more than 50 secondary ISP interconnections, covering Chinese Mainland and other major markets across Asia Pacific, North America, Latin America, the Middle East, and Europe. From supporting Tencent's own large-scale gaming, audio and video, and e-commerce businesses to serving enterprises across industries worldwide, EdgeOne brings decades of experience in global edge infrastructure and supports sectors including finance, gaming, media, e-commerce and new retail, logistics, ticketing, aviation, and hospitality. It provides a technology foundation for enterprises expanding globally and entering the Chinese market. Empowering the Gaming Industry with Low-Latency Delivery According to IDC's China Gaming Cloud Market Tracker, H1 2025, Tencent Cloud CDN services powered by EdgeOne have ranked first in China by revenue for four consecutive years. Gaming resource delivery volume has also ranked first. EdgeOne has supported the distribution and security of Farlight 84, which attracted over 16 million pre-registrations ahead of launch, and Mecha BREAK, which registered over 5.2 million players for its global open beta. It has also defended Delta Force against hundreds of attacks. Meanwhile, EdgeOne Booster provides edge inference capabilities for emerging use cases such as AI-powered Non-Player Characters (NPCs), intelligent recommendations, and real-time content generation, bringing computing resources closer to players and enhancing real-time interactive experiences. Accelerating Audio & Video Content Delivery Globally EdgeOne covers 80% of the top 10 China-based outbound audio and video social applications by scale and serves leading global customers including Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME), Japanese karaoke app Pokekara, and Pakistani internet TV platform ARY ZAP. As AI reshapes content production and interactive experiences, EdgeOne Booster enables open-source multimodal models to be deployed at the edge, allowing images, video, and audio assets to be generated and processed closer to users without being sent back to centralized cloud infrastructure. This significantly shortens the AI content production workflow and provides global media businesses with high-concurrency, low-latency edge inference capabilities. Driving Conversions for E-commerce and New Retail with AI EdgeOne Makers enables one-stop deployment and hosting of e-commerce AI agents, helping AI move from "answering questions" to "solving problems." Across customer service, logistics tracking, returns and exchanges, and product selection and marketing, AI agents can execute business tasks directly, providing 24/7 service and improving operational efficiency for global businesses. Beyond the IDC MarketScape, Tencent Cloud has also been recognized as a representative vendor in three Gartner Market Guides covering Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) mitigation solutions, web application and API protection (WAAP), and edge distribution platforms, with related capabilities incorporated into the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) international standards. From accelerating and protecting the internet to connecting AI computing and powering AI applications, Tencent Cloud EdgeOne continues to extend its global network, security, and edge computing capabilities for the AI era, helping enterprises across industries connect with users worldwide and bring AI-powered businesses into production. The framework also provides technology buyers with a 360-degree assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of current and prospective suppliers. ### About Tencent Cloud Tencent Cloud is one of the world's fastest-growing cloud service providers, committed to delivering innovative solutions that address everyday life and business challenges, and empowering the digital transformation of smart industries. title: Sacked massage therapist who glassed a workmate fails to win her job back after claiming there was much more to the story
description: Amorn Bangpa, who worked for Vimana Thai Massage for more than two years, launched a bid for unfair dismissal with the Fair Work Commission.
content: - See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source A Thai massage therapist who smashed a glass over a colleague's head has failed to get her job back after arguing she did not start the workplace fight. Amorn Bangpa, who worked for Vimana Thai Massage for more than two years, launched a bid for unfair dismissal with the Fair Work Commission. Her case was dismissed after she missed the statutory deadline and filed her claim 16 days late, arguing criminal proceedings arising from the incident had consumed her time and caused significant stress. The experienced Thai traditional medicine practitioner was arrested by NSW Police following the workplace altercation on June 14. Ms Bangpa pleaded guilty to assault occasioning actual bodily harm and was handed a conditional release order without conviction in July, despite saying she was provoked. She told the Commission the workplace incident had been taken out of context. While she acknowledged a glass struck her colleague's head during the altercation, Ms Bangpa argued the employer's account omitted the events that led up to it. She said she had been unwell with acute bronchitis and was drinking warm water to soothe a sore throat and persistent cough when a verbal dispute broke out with two co-workers. FWC Deputy President Alexandra Grayson ruled there were no exceptional circumstances warranting an extension for a massage therapist sacked over an assault on a colleague (stock image) According to Ms Bangpa, she tried to defuse the situation by asking one colleague to stop verbally abusing her, but the woman instead jabbed at her face. Ms Bangpa said she then splashed water at the colleague in an attempt to make her back away, prompting the woman to scratch, bruise, kick and attempt to slap her. She claimed she reacted instinctively to the alleged attack and did not intend to injure her colleague. The other employee in the incident called police, and submitted a statement the following day which resulted in criminal charges being brought against Ms Bangpa. Their police statement claimed Ms Bangpa picked up a glass and smashed it onto the other worker's head, causing pain, headache, blurred vision and some memory loss. The colleague, who was not charged, suffered a two-centimetre cut, swelling and tenderness on the scalp, 'consistent with having been hit on the head by something'. Ms Bangpa had a superficial abrasion and two bruises on her right upper arm. She claimed prior to her dismissal, the massage parlour's owner had received incorrect information from police suggesting she had a prior criminal record and relied on that information when deciding to terminate her employment. Amorn Bangpa, who worked for Vimana Thai Massage for more than two years, launched a bid for unfair dismissal with the Fair Work Commission (stock image) She told the Fair Work Commission she had been unfairly dismissed because of the alleged misinformation and was not given an opportunity to respond or provide evidence showing she had no prior criminal record. Ms Bangpa also claimed her employer failed to properly consider her explanation, did not carry out a formal disciplinary investigation and treated her unfairly because the other worker involved in the altercation kept her job. In its response to the Fair Work Commission, Vimana Thai Massage said Ms Bangpa was sacked for the attack and argued the conduct amounted to serious misconduct and maintained she was not dismissed because of any alleged criminal history. Ms Bangpa told the Fair Work Commission the criminal case dominated her life following her dismissal and contributed to the late filing of her application. She said the court case, coupled with what she described as false accusations circulating on social media, caused her significant emotional distress. At the hearing, Ms Bangpa said she was shocked and devastated by the outcome of the criminal charges and believed police had relied on a distorted version of events provided by the other party involved in the altercation. Despite missing the Fair Work filing deadline by just 16 days, Deputy President Alexandra Grayson ruled there were no exceptional circumstances warranting an extension. She said while it was clear Ms Bangpa had engaged in violent behaviour in the workplace, 'the context of that violence is less clear'. 'There is no medical evidence which demonstrates any ill effects on Ms Bangpa's mental health or capacity to be involved in legal proceedings or lodge the application,' Ms Grayson said in her published decision. 'Whilst I accept that this would have been a stressful time for Ms Bangpa, I conclude that feelings of stress and/or anxiety after a dismissal, or after being charged with a criminal offence, are not unusual or exceptional. 'Whilst I also accept that Ms Bangpa's involvement in the criminal proceedings would have been time consuming and required a lot of attention from her, I do not consider that this provides a credible or reasonable explanation for the delay. 'Ms Bangpa was not on remand. There is no evidence that this process consumed Ms Bangpa day and night. She was legally represented for at least some of the criminal proceedings, and could rely on her representatives in those proceedings.'

title: Saudi Arabia shoots down Houthi drone strike outside of Mecca
description: The attacks on Saudi Arabia have shocked global energy markets roiled by the six-month US-Iran war, which has slowed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to a trickle.
content: Saudi Arabia’s air defenses destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen said on Wednesday, as fighting spreads in the Middle East. The drone, intercepted on Tuesday evening, was the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca after a ballistic missile launch in July 2017, spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a statement, and follows a week of attacks from Iran-aligned Houthi fighters that have drawn Saudi Arabia deeper into the war. Mecca is home to some of the holiest sites in Islam and the focal point of the annual hajj pilgrimage, and its security was a “red line,” the coalition spokesperson al-Malki said in the statement. Houthi officials have denied targeting Mecca. The attacks on Saudi Arabia have shocked global energy markets roiled by the six-month US-Iran war, which has slowed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to a trickle. The Houthis have seized control of parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast in recent days overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb, one of the world’s most important shipping straits, threatening Saudi Arabia’s oil exports rerouted from the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia issued security alerts for Mecca on Tuesday, but Houthi political bureau member Mohammed al-Farah denied the group had targeted the city, calling the allegation “an outright lie” in comments carried by the Houthi-run SABA news agency. The Houthis have announced several major attacks on Saudi Arabia over the past week, including attacks on an air base on Monday, which they said were in retaliation for airstrikes on Yemen. The air base attack wounded 13 civilians, Saudi-led military coalition officials said. Saudi Arabia has blamed a separate pro-Iranian movement, based in Iraq, for an attack on Friday that knocked out one of the kingdom’s most important oil transport routes, the East-West Pipeline across the Arabian desert. The 745-mile East-West Pipeline linking Saudi Arabia’s Gulf oil fields to the Red Sea has been the kingdom’s principal export route while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted by nearly seven months of war, which has killed thousands of people across the region. Since the pipeline was shut after Friday’s attack, traders say a prolonged closure could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume. But US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days. Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since 2015. The conflict had largely quieted under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis pushed back forces aligned with the Yemeni government this month. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned US President Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so far has been limited to intelligence aid.

title: Stories for an emerging food system
description: The podcast Farmerama Radio is celebrating 10 years of regenerative farming, storytelling and community building.
content: Stories do more than document change – they can help bring new systems into being. Ten years of Farmerama, ten years of sharing the voices behind regenerative farming. And I feel more certain than ever about the importance of this work. My family started farming on 10 hectares in Chile after I went to university – it was a real baptism of fire. By the time I co-founded Farmerama, we had planted a few thousand olive trees and had many unanswered questions about how to farm ‘beyond organic’, as we called it at the time. I had attended a few farming events in the UK and realised there were many people already farming in this way who we could learn from – it just wasn’t easy to uncover their stories. This article first appeared in the latest issue of the Resurgence & Ecologist print magazine. Market Making a podcast felt like the perfect way to ask questions while simultaneously sharing the learning with others. From the beginning, we set out to champion farmers and landworkers already crafting a more ecological future. Every season brings new opportunities to find better ways of working with the ecosystems they tend, and we wanted to share those experiments and what they learned. These farmers, often small-scale and working closely with natural systems, stood in stark contrast to the industrial, chemical-based farm systems that have become the norm and are often thick with mud and largely devoid of life. It’s also important to recognise what we learned early on: most farmers, ecological or otherwise, are genuinely trying to feed people. They are far from villains in this story. Rather, their systems have been shaped by market forces and government policy over recent decades. Many find themselves locked into those systems, carrying substantial debt from infrastructure or machinery that was innovative at the time. Future In one of our earliest episodes, we spoke with organic grower Ian Tolhurst about his experiments using woodchips to create biologically active, fungal-dominant compost, and even growing outdoor salads on compost heaps through the UK winter. At the time, very little was widely understood about woodchip composts, and soil science was only just cottoning on to the value of having lots of fungi in the soil – particularly for growing trees and vines. Just over five years later, we spoke with farmer Ben Raskin, head of agroforestry at the Soil Association, about his – somewhat accidental – experiments in agroforestry with deep woodchip mulch around trees. These led to trees growing almost four times larger, insights that led him to write The Woodchip Handbook. We continue to learn more each year about the importance of fungi in soils, and often it feels as though soil scientists are learning directly from farmers who are pushing these boundaries. Stories do more than document change – they can help bring new systems into being. As we heard so often in those early years, sharing the voices of people on land and sea, all working towards a better future, helped those farming in often isolated rural places to learn from others and feel part of a much wider movement. Incredulous This collective was working to build soil health and biodiversity, to grow healthy nutritious food, to regenerate water cycles, and to nourish people both physically and emotionally. In 2019, we tried an experiment of our own. I had recently been part of an art project called A Field of Wheat, created by Anne-Marie Culhane and Ruth Levene – a truly life-changing experience. To participate, I invested £200 in a 20-acre field of wheat on farmer Peter Lundgren’s farm in Lincolnshire, along with around 40 other people. It was an eclectic group, including heritage grain experts, fertiliser specialists, an agricultural bank manager, and people like me whose only real connection with wheat was the bread I ate weekly. We used Quaker principles to collectively discuss and make farming decisions online. I completely shocked myself by voting not to follow organic principles, but to apply nitrogen to the crop in late spring. After years of buying organic food and being incredulous that any farmer would choose synthetics, here I was doing exactly that. Knowledge-sharing I made the decision after hearing that, due to the genetics of the wheat we had sown, the likelihood of total crop failure was very high if we did not apply nitrogen. The farmer had also invested 50 per cent of the money in the field, so he had far more to lose than the rest of us. It was a humbling experience, and there were many more moments in the decision-making process where I was taken aback – from the seeds we were legally allowed to plant and grow to the unachievable “protein” targets required to mill the wheat into flour for human consumption. At every turn, it seemed we were locked into a commodity system whether we liked it or not. Around the same time, I met Kimberley Bell, founder of Small Food Bakery, and learned about her work using the genetically diverse wheat YQ (Yield-Quality), developed by the legendary Martin Wolfe, to bake delicious bread. It turned out that this was part of a local grains economy taking shape in the UK. Given our proximity to this work and the understanding we had built, it made sense to create a long-form investigative podcast unearthing the constraints of the current commodity bread system, and the people in the UK powering this ‘new grains’ movement. This became our first in-depth series, Cereal, which traced how the current system came about in a logical way, but had become a trap with some illogical outcomes – just as I had experienced in A Field of Wheat. We followed breeders, scientists, bakers, millers and farmers who are working to build a new, localised system based on knowledge-sharing and transparency, opening up a whole web of possibilities for growing and processing cereals. Batches Long-time organic farmer Mark Lea was brought to tears as he took a bite of a YQ loaf baked by Bell – his first ever taste of the wheat he had grown. When Cereal came out, we were inundated with people sharing the impact listening had on their lives. Farmers got in touch asking how they could grow these population wheats (or genetically diverse varieties). Bakers around the world wrote in sharing stories of finding and building local grain systems. People seemed genuinely shocked, as I had been, about this part of the food system that we all participate in, often without realising it. Many were also feeling trapped in the commodity system and wanted the opportunity to get out and do something different. Over this past year, we decided to dig deeper into the impact of the series through a research project and podcast we called Cereal Revisited. We were curious to understand why it struck such a chord, as well as to celebrate the listeners who took action, big or small, off the back of it. We heard from engineer Emma Shires how Cereal helped her understand that, in order for local grains to reach bakers, we needed millers across the country who could process small batches of these wheats – so she decided to start a whole new career as a miller, and now runs a milling business providing flours to bakers in the Nottingham area. Voice We also heard from farmers Tom and Mary Edmondson, who told us how they have shifted their business away from commodities and started milling their own grain on farm, baking bread, and setting up a farm shop supplying their local community. So much of mainstream media focuses on the ‘hero’s journey’ – the struggles and successes of individuals – but Cereal was something different, and it had a transformational impact that the hero’s journey alone cannot achieve. There was no call to action, yet it has been incredibly powerful to see how people become curious enough to engage in their own ways – whether that be reaching out to connect to a farmer, setting up a network of like-minded bakers, returning to university for a degree in food systems, or setting off on a pilgrimage to meet the changemakers and pioneers farming differently. This emergent system is still very small and there are many challenges ahead, from the need to permanently update UK law so that we can legally breed and trade these genetically diverse seeds to experimenting with new organisational structures because profit-focused business models tend to derail the good intentions of the emerging system. No one person or perspective holds the answer. But by giving voice to radical ideas, experiments, failures and successes, people discover they have permission to get stuck in. This Author Abby Rose is a farmer and storyteller. She is the co-founder, co-producer and co-host of Farmerama Radio, an award-winning podcast sharing the voices behind regenerative farming. Each month, the show features farmers and growers rebuilding our food and ecosystems from the ground up. You can check out Farmerama’s new project Cereal Revisited online. This article first appeared in the latest issue of the Resurgence & Ecologist print magazine.

title: Nifty holds above 23,250 level; European shares trade mostly in green
description: The benchmark indices traded near the day's high in afternoon trade, tracking positive cues from Asian markets as the recent rally in crude oil prices paused. Investors remained cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserves policy meeting later today. The Nifty s…
content: Nifty holds above 23,250 level; European shares trade mostly in green The benchmark indices traded near the day's high in afternoon trade, tracking positive cues from Asian markets as the recent rally in crude oil prices paused. Investors remained cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserves policy meeting later today. The Nifty surged above the 23,250 mark, indicating some recovery in market sentiment. At 13:21 IST, the barometer index, the S&P BSE Sensex jumped 425.42 points or 0.57% to 74,429.24. The Nifty 50 index added 141.90 points or 0.61% to 23,260.50. In the broader market, the BSE 150 MidCap Index rose 0.19% and the BSE 250 SmallCap Index shed 0.06%. The market breadth was negative. On the BSE, 1,832 shares rose and 2,320 shares fell. A total of 271 shares were unchanged. Economy: Also Read India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) will roll out a targeted Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) regime effective 15 October 2026, ending a years-long blanket zero-MDR policy to build a self-sustaining funding base for network infrastructure, cybersecurity, and platform scalability. Under the new guidelines notified by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and the Reserve Bank of India, a standard 0.4% MDRcapped at Rs 300 for high-ticket purchaseswill apply strictly to commercial person-to-merchant (P2M) payments above Rs 2,000, while essential utilities and fuel will draw a flat Rs 5 fee and capital market transfers are levied at 0.02%. Retail consumers and individual peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers remain entirely insulated from charges, as do small merchants processing under Rs 1 lakh a month and all transactions up to Rs 2,000, which together account for over 95% of daily UPI transaction volumes. Indias current account deficit widened to $11.2 billion during April-July 2026 from $6.6 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier, mainly due to a higher merchandise trade deficit. The goods trade gap increased to $117.8 billion in the first four months of the financial year from $97.1 billion a year ago, as imports grew faster than exports. Meanwhile, net services receipts rose to $69.3 billion from $64.3 billion in April-July 2025. Gainers & Losers: ITC (up 2.19%), Tata Consumer (up 2.14%), Trent (up 2.12%), SBI (up 2.08%) and Nestle India (up 1.98%) were the top gainers. TCS (down 1.88%), Wipro (down 1.51%), Tech Mahindra (down 1.15%), Infosys (down 1.13%) and Indigo (down 0.92%) were the top losers. Stocks in Spotlight: Equitas Small Finance Bank rose 1.01%. The bank said that its board has approved a proposal to raise funds aggregating to Rs 500 crore through the issuance of non-convertible debentures. Alkem Laboratories rose 0.18%. The company has announced the launch of NeuCeno (cenobamate), anti-seizure medication (ASM) for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in adult patients. Praj Industries fell 1.04%. The company said that it signed a development & commercialization agreement for bio-isobutanol (Bio-IBA) technology in India. Under the agreement, Praj will lead the commercialization of Bio-IBA technology in India, with exclusive rights to deploy the technology in the country. Allied Blenders and Distillers advanced 0.74%. The company said that it has been granted a licence for manufacture of malt spirits for potable purpose by the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise, Telangana, Hyderabad. Global Markets: European equities edged marginally higher while most Asian equity benchmarks traded higher on Wednesday, supported by regional gains ahead of the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement. The upward movement occurred alongside elevated crude oil prices and higher US Treasury yields. In Japan, trade deficit widened significantly to JPY 1,105.6 billion in August 2026 from JPY 294.1 billion a year earlier. It marked the fourth consecutive month of deficit and the largest since January, as imports grew faster than exports. Imports surged 28.0% year-on-year to JPY 11,153.9 billion, following a 27.9% rise in July, marking the strongest growth since November 2022. Exports rose 19.3% to JPY 10,048.4 billion. US indices declined on Tuesday, driven by positioning ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting and rising bond yields. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 328.09 points, or 0.63%, to 52,093.11; the S&P 500 declined 0.45% to 7,585.73; and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.78% to 25,981.57. Certain technology shares recorded advances, with Qualcomm gaining over 4%, and Advanced Micro Devices and Coherent each rising approximately 2%. The Federal Reserve is scheduled to release its interest rate decision on Wednesday. Market pricing reflects expectations of a 25-basis-point increase from the existing target range of 3.5% to 3.75%. Market attention is focused on the policy statement and accompanying commentary regarding inflation, economic conditions, and projected interest rate adjustments. title: Real estate transactions nearly double in one year
description: Kathmandu, Sept 16: Real estate transactions in Nepal nearly doubled within a year, according to data released Tuesday by the Economic Research Department of Nepal Rastra Bank. The figures show a sharp increase in the value of property transactions in the las…
content: Kathmandu, Sept 16: Real estate transactions in Nepal nearly doubled within a year, according to data released Tuesday by the Economic Research Department of Nepal Rastra Bank. The figures show a sharp increase in the value of property transactions in the last fiscal year compared with the previous year. Property transactions worth Rs 386.15 billion were recorded in fiscal year 2024/25, rising to Rs 720.86 billion in fiscal year 2025/26. The number of transactions fell by 1.84 per cent in 2024/25 but increased by 4.74 per cent in 2025/26. Nepal currently has 32.847 million registered land plots. Officials at the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation have viewed the rise in real estate transactions positively despite restrictions on land subdivision in local units that have not completed land classification. Although the market showed signs of renewed activity after the election, transactions slowed somewhat during the early months of the current fiscal year, particularly in Shrawan, Ashoj and Kartik. According to the department, 22 land revenue offices and 14 survey offices were damaged by arson and vandalism during the recent unrest. All of the affected offices have since been repaired and resumed operations. More recently, the government’s campaign to remove middlemen from land revenue and survey offices has led to the arrest of deed writers, triggering protests. Officials and market participants have expressed concern that the dispute could affect the recovery of the property market. The data also shows a steady increase in women’s ownership of real estate. The number of female landowners across the country has reached 4.483 million, accounting for 39 per cent of the total. In urban areas, women now account for around 50 per cent of landowners. Of the country’s total registered land plots, 22.024 million are registered in men’s names and 9.762 million in women’s names. Data for fiscal year 2023/24 showed that women’s and men’s participation in land purchases and sales was almost equal, with 400,241 women and 403,451 men involved in such transactions. title: Semaglutide Prices Keep Moving. Here's Why Nobody Can Give You a Straight Answer
description: Semaglutide pricing varies widely by insurance, pharmacy and eligibility for discounts. Branded list prices remain high, while coverage rules, savings caps and compounding changes affect affordability.
content: Semaglutide Prices Keep Moving. Here's Why Nobody Can Give You a Straight Answer A pharmacist in suburban Chicago told a reporter last year that she gets asked the same question probably ten times a day, and she still doesn't have a clean answer for it. Patients want to know what they'll actually pay before they commit to a prescription, and the honest response involves at least four variables she has no control over. That's a strange place for healthcare to sit in 2025, but it's where Semaglutide pricing has landed. The List Price Isn't What Most People Pay, But It's Still the Starting Point Ozempic and Wegovy both list around $935 to $1,350 a month depending on dose and formulation, and that number gets quoted constantly in news coverage. It's rarely the number that shows up on anyone's actual receipt. Insurance negotiates its own rate. PBMs extract rebates. Manufacturer coupons chip away at what commercially insured patients owe out of pocket. So when someone asks how much does Semaglutide cost, the accurate answer usually starts with "it depends on your coverage," which is unsatisfying but true. Insurance Coverage Has Gotten More Restrictive, Not Less This is the part that surprises a lot of patients. Given how much attention these drugs get, you'd expect coverage to be expanding. In several cases it's tightening. More insurers now require documented failed attempts at other weight-loss methods before approving Wegovy for obesity. Some employer plans that covered it broadly in 2023 have since added prior authorization requirements or capped the benefit entirely after watching their pharmacy spend triple in a single plan year. A benefits director quoted in a Kaiser Family Foundation survey put it bluntly: uncapped GLP-1 coverage was never sustainable at the utilization rates plans were seeing. Medicare still doesn't cover Wegovy for weight loss, only for cardiovascular risk reduction in patients who meet specific criteria, which excludes a lot of people who'd otherwise qualify based on BMI alone. Compounded Versions Created a Temporary Workaround That's Mostly Gone Now For roughly two years, compounding pharmacies sold Semaglutide at a fraction of branded pricing under an FDA provision that permits compounding during a drug shortage. Prices ran $150 to $300 a month in a lot of cases, which made the drug accessible to patients who had no realistic path to the branded version. Once the FDA declared the Semaglutide shortage resolved in early 2025, that legal cover started disappearing, and most compounders had to stop selling it or shift to a much narrower justification tied to personalized dosing. Patients who'd built a treatment plan around that pricing got caught off guard when their usual source suddenly wasn't an option.It was never a stable long-term solution. It just felt like one while the shortage lasted. Novo Nordisk's Direct-to-Consumer Pricing Changed the Conversation In 2024, Novo Nordisk launched a self-pay option for Wegovy through NovoCare, priced around $499 a month for patients without insurance coverage, roughly half the list price. This mattered more than it initially got credit for. It gave uninsured patients a legitimate alternative to compounded versions right as those were becoming harder to access, and it put pressure on the broader pricing conversation in a way that a simple coupon never could. Eli Lilly followed a similar path with Zepbound around the same time, which suggests this kind of direct pricing is becoming a permanent fixture rather than a temporary promotion. Savings Cards Help, Until the Fine Print Kicks In Manufacturer savings cards can bring a commercially insured patient's cost down to $25 a month, and for a lot of people, that's the number that actually determines whether the drug is affordable at all. But these programs usually cap total annual savings, often somewhere around $2,000, and once a patient hits that cap, they're facing something much closer to full price for the rest of the year. Patients on Medicare or Medicaid typically don't qualify at all, which means the people with the least financial flexibility are often the ones excluded from the best discount available. Final Thought Every price quoted in this space is really a snapshot of one moment in a market that's still working itself out, shaped by shortage rules, insurer risk tolerance, and manufacturer strategy that shifts every few months. Anyone treating a single number as the definitive answer is missing the point. The number that matters is the one specific to your coverage, your pharmacy, and this particular week, and it's worth checking again before assuming last year's price still holds. © Copyright 2026 IBTimes AU. title: Anthropic signs first Australian data centre lease
description: Anthropic has signed its first lease for data center capacity in Australia, at a site on a campus planned for farmland, about 250km west of Brisbane, according to Reuters, which cited two people familiar with the deal.  The site on which the data center will …
content: Anthropic has signed its first lease for data center capacity in Australia, at a site on a campus planned for farmland, about 250km west of Brisbane, according to Reuters, which cited two people familiar with the deal. The site on which the data center will be built belongs to a Singapore-based developer, likely Zerra DC, and plans are to reach 2.16 GW, close enough to rank among the largest computing campuses. Also, neither the value or financial terms nor the length of the lease was disclosed, and the deal still needs sign-off from Australia’s Foreign Investment Review Board. What we know so far is that the facility will handle only inference, or rapid, prediction-based processing, running models that have already been trained rather than training new ones, the same sources told Reuters. But this news is not new to Anthropic, as the company spent most of the year circling Australia. In a visit to Canberra in March, Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, signed a government memorandum of understanding, saying it was “exploring investments in data center infrastructure and energy throughout the country.” Emails later obtained by the ABC showed that, before the same trip, the company had asked New South Wales officials about installing up to 5GW of AI training capacity in the state. For Anthropic, the recent lease in Queensland is the latest in a series of significant infrastructure investments, following a substantial $45bn Nscale deal in Britain and a 20-year Riot contract in the US. The project’s location puts it at the center of Australia’s debate over who should pay to power these facilities. Canberra is working on national energy rules that would make large data centers buy electricity from new renewable projects. Meanwhile, Queensland Premier David Crisafulli wants standards that still allow for gas and coal. Zerra’s site is next to three gas-fired power stations, as well as solar and wind farms. Before any of this can happen, Canberra’s foreign investment regulator needs to approve the deal, and the Dalby council must also agree. title: Giredmet inks pact with Alt Metals for titanium sponge pilot production unit
description: Russia’s State Research and Design Institute of Rare Metal Industry (Giredmet) has signed a contract with Alt Metals to establish a pilot production facility for titanium sponge, the primary feedstock for making titanium.
content: Russia’s State Research and Design Institute of Rare Metal Industry (Giredmet) has signed a contract with Alt Metals to establish a pilot production facility for titanium sponge, the primary feedstock for making titanium. Titanium, which is valued for its strength, lightness and corrosion resistance, is used to make alloys and components for industries such as Defence, aerospace, medical devices, among others. The pact between Giredmet and Alt Metals was signed at the Innoprom India exhibition in New Delhi last week. It aims to develop cooperation between Russian and Indian specialists in the field of deep processing of mineral raw materials and provides for the supply of laboratory equipment for the production of titanium sponge. “This relates to developing the initial design data for industrial titanium sponge production with a capacity of 1,000 tonnes per year. During the first stage, we will conduct a study of the customer’s raw materials, conduct laboratory testing, manufacture and supply a set of laboratory equipment, and provide installation supervision, commissioning, and personnel training. We are interested in scaling the technology to industrial scale and subsequently integrating it into Indian industry,” said Andrey Goliney, Director of the Chemical Engineering Division at Rosatom Nauka JSC (the managing organisation of Giredmet JSC). Giredmet is part of Rosatom State Atomic Energy Corporation of Russia--a nuclear energy solutions behemoth. It covers the full cycle--from developing enrichment methods for ores containing rare and rare-earth metals to producing high-purity substances, single crystals, and finished products for the electronics, nuclear, aviation, and space industries. Russia is consistently developing international trade and economic relations, focusing on cooperation with friendly countries. The domestic economy is increasing its export potential, supplying goods, services, and raw materials worldwide. Rosatom and its enterprises are actively involved in this work. Giredmet is already working with TEXMiN Foundation (Technology Translation Research Park) on joint R&D initiatives to develop NdFeB rare-earth permanent magnet technologies. TEXMiN is a section-8 company created under a programme by the Department of Science and Technology at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad. In May this year, TEXMiN and Giredmet signed a Statement of Intent (SoI) to strengthen bilateral cooperation in rare earth permanent magnet technologies, critical minerals, and advanced metallurgical research. Neodymium-Iron-Boron (NdFeB) rare earth permanent magnets are key intermediate components of permanent magnet synchronous (direct drive) generators in wind turbines (especially for offshore turbines) and electric synchronous traction motors for propulsion systems in battery and hybrid electric vehicles (EVs). title: Pete Alonso Reaches 300-Home Run Milestone Against His Old Team
description: Pete Alonso launched his 300th career home run, a tying shot in the ninth inning against his former team.
content: Pete Alonso Reaches 300-Home Run Milestone Against His Old Team Pete Alonso launched his 300th career home run Tuesday night, a tying shot in the ninth inning against his former team, and Coby Mayo’s inside-the-park homer in the 11th sent the Baltimore Orioles to a 7-5 victory over the New York Mets. Christian Encarnacion-Strand and Jeremiah Jackson also went deep for the Orioles (74-78), who stayed three games behind Cleveland for the last American League playoff spot. Mayo snapped a 4-all tie with a three-run homer in the 11th. He connected on an 0-2 pitch from Jonathan Pintaro with two outs and sent a long drive to center field that glanced off rookie A.J. Ewing's glove as he crashed into the fence. The ball rolled away from Ewing as he fell to the ground, allowing Mayo to circle the bases and score standing up. Alonso, who hit a club-record 264 homers for the Mets before signing with the Orioles last December, was hitless in his first seven plate appearances of the series before launching a 414-foot solo drive off Kodai Senga to tie the score at 3 with one out in the ninth. A pumped-up Alonso spiked his bat toward the Orioles dugout and rounded the bases as the Citi Field crowd of 28,097 — down from 35,800 on Monday — roared. Fans chanted his name until Alonso emerged from the dugout for a curtain call, after which chants of "Fire Stearns" aimed at Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns began. It was Senga’s first blown save in eight chances this season. The teams traded runs in the 10th, when Encarnacion-Strand raced home on a wild pitch and Marcus Semien laced a one-out RBI double for the Mets. Alonso struck out against Pintaro (2-2) in the 11th before Mayo’s inside-the-park homer made a winner of Alex Hoppe (1-1). Andrew Kittredge earned his 10th save after allowing Bo Bichette’s two-out RBI single. New York (69-82) lost its third straight and was assured of a losing season. Carson Benge homered for the Mets, eliminated from playoff contention with Monday’s 2-1 loss to Baltimore. Jared Young had a sacrifice fly and Juan Soto delivered an RBI single. Up next Orioles RHP Chris Bassitt (7-5, 4.88 ERA) starts Wednesday’s series finale against Mets RHP Robert Stock (1-3, 5.93).

title: ‘Let’s not seek change for sake of change,’ Oba of Benin backs continuity
description:
“In democracy there must be opposition when a party comes to power. I don't see why an opposition party can't support the ruling party” 
The post ‘Let’s not seek change for sake of change,’ Oba of Benin backs continuity appeared first on Vanguard News.
content: Oba of Benin, His Royal Majesty Omo N’Oba N’Edo Uku Akpolokpolo Oba Ewuare II (middle) and members of the Presidential Campaign Council led by its Director-General, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, during the courtesy visit to the Palace of the Oba of Benin on Tuesday. By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — The Oba of Benin, His Majesty, Omo N’Oba N’Edo Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, on Tuesday urged opposition parties in Nigeria not to be extremely critical of the ruling party, but to play their role as opposition for the betterment of the country. Read Also: 2027: APC govs at daggers-drawn with Wike The Benin monarch also urged Nigerians to support continuity in governance and not seek change just for the sake of change. The monarch spoke on Tuesday when the Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Abdulaziz Yari, led members of the council to the Benin Palace to seek royal blessings, prayers and support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. Oba Ewuare II said the Benin throne was not partisan, adding that his position should not be interpreted as support for any political party. “The Benin throne is not partisan. There is no point for change for the sake of change. That is not to say that I belong to one party or the other. “Is there anybody who is as perfect as I am talking now? Nobody. I love and like peace and tranquillity. I am American and British trained as a diplomat, and I say it the way it is,” he said. Oba Ewuare II also appealed to former governors, senators and other political leaders to work together in the interest of the country, stressing the importance of cooperation between the ruling party and the opposition. “In democracy there must be opposition when a party comes to power. I don’t see why an opposition party can’t support the ruling party,” he said. Earlier, Yari said the mission of the council to the palace was to seek royal blessings, prayers and support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, whom he described as the monarch’s son. The former Zamfara State governor said the Tinubu administration had made progress in the economy, citing changes in GDP growth, inflation and foreign exchange stability. Yari said Nigeria’s annual GDP growth had risen from 2.7 per cent in 2023 to 3.9 per cent, while inflation had declined from 22.9 per cent to 15.9 per cent. He added that the administration had stabilised the foreign exchange market and described Tinubu as the right person to lead the country. Also, the Deputy Governor of Edo State, who stood in for Governor Monday Okpebholo, Rt. Hon. Dennis Idahosa, thanked the Oba of Benin for his royal blessings, noting that the President deserved a second term and that Southern Nigeria also deserved a second term. “For us in Edo State, Governor Monday Okpebholo is the leader and he is leading well as we have a lot of projects to campaign with and the people of Edo State will vote massively for President Tinubu to enable him win the 2027 Presidential election”. In Yari’s entourage were the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Sen. George Akume; former Kano State Governor, Abdullahi Umar Ganduje; former Katsina State Governor, Aminu Bello Masari; and former Borno State Governor, Ali Modu Sheriff. Also in the delegation were former President of the Senate, Pius Ayim; Hon. James Faleke; Sunday Sunday Dare; Abdul’malik Zubairu; Prof. Joseph Terlumun; Professor Ussiju Medaner Al-Mustapha; Lawal Funtua; Lawal M. Liman; Muhammad Gololo; and Nasiruddeen Abdul’aziz Yari.

title: OpenAI eyes $1.2 trillion valuation in fresh funding round as IPO slips to 2027
description: OpenAI is reportedly in early discussions with investors for a new funding round that could value the ChatGPT maker at around $1.2 trillion. The move comes months after its $122 billion fundraise and as CEO Sam Altman pushes the company’s IPO timeline to 2027.
content:
AI could be heading for another major valuation jump even as the ChatGPT maker puts its stock market debut on hold. The company is in early discussions with investors about a potential new funding round that could value it at around $1.2 trillion, the Financial Times reported. The talks are in the early stages and could still change, but the reported figure would represent a significant increase over OpenAI’s most recent valuation. In March, OpenAI raised $122 billion in what was then a record-setting funding round, giving the company a post-money valuation of about $852 billion. A $1.2 trillion valuation would represent an increase of roughly 41% from that level. The latest discussions also come at an interesting time for OpenAI. CEO Sam Altman has indicated that the company is unlikely to pursue an initial public offering (IPO) in 2026. He has cited concerns about the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems and said that focusing on safety and alignment is more important at present. OpenAI had confidentially filed IPO paperwork earlier this year, with 2027 now emerging as the more likely timeline. A fresh private fundraise could give OpenAI access to additional capital without requiring the company to immediately enter public markets. That matters because developing increasingly sophisticated AI models is an expensive business. OpenAI spent about $34 billion last year, according to the Financial Times, while its annualised revenue crossed $40 billion last month following the launch of newer products. The fundraising discussions also underline the enormous amount of money still flowing into the AI industry despite growing concerns about valuations, infrastructure costs and the risks associated with rapid development. OpenAI is facing intense competition from Anthropic, which has also attracted substantial investor interest and is preparing for a potential public listing. The rivalry between the two companies has increasingly become a race not only for AI models and customers but also for access to capital. For OpenAI, another large private round would provide more financial firepower as it continues investing in model development and computing infrastructure. It could also allow existing and new investors to increase their exposure before the company eventually enters public markets. However, the reported $1.2 trillion figure remains a potential valuation rather than a completed transaction. The discussions are preliminary, and there is no confirmed fundraising size or closing date yet. The bigger question for investors is what happens when OpenAI eventually moves from private-market valuations to public-market scrutiny. Until then, another private round could give the ChatGPT maker more time—and more capital—to scale its AI ambitions before asking public investors to put a price on the company. Anjali Thakur is a Senior Assistant Editor with Mint, reporting on trending news, entertainment and health, with a focus on stories driving digital conversations. Her work involves spotting early signals across news cycles and social media, sharpening stories for SEO and Google Discover, and mentoring young editors in digital-first newsroom practices. She is known for turning fast-moving developments—whether news-driven or culture-led—into clear, tightly edited journalism without compromising editorial rigour.

Before joining Mint, she was Deputy News Editor at NDTV.com, where she led the Trending section and covered viral news, breaking developments and human-interest stories. She has also worked as Chief Sub-Editor at India.com (Zee Media) and as Senior Correspondent with Exchange4media and Hindustan Times’ HT City, reporting on media, advertising, entertainment, health, lifestyle and popular culture.

Anjali holds a Bachelor of Arts degree from Miranda House, and is currently pursuing an MBA, strengthening her understanding of business strategy and digital media economics. Her writing balances newsroom discipline with a clear instinct for what resonates with readers.

title: Houthis seize strategic Red Sea islands as analysts warn of impending oil crunch
description: Militant group in Yemen captured the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish, near the chokepoint of the Bab al-Mandab strait
content: Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen, Houthi militants said on Wednesday, as the Iran-backed fighters solidified their gains following a lightning advance that has extended Tehran’s reach in the Middle East war and further disrupted global oil supplies. The Iran-backed Houthis, who since last week have swept through Yemeni towns along the Red Sea coast and seized islands in the Bab el-Mandeb strait at its mouth, released battlefield video overnight of fighters seizing armoured vehicles from Saudi-backed forces. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had launched fresh drone and missile strikes on the main Saudi Red Sea oil port of Yanbu, and at a southern Saudi airbase at Khamis Mushait. He did not say when the strikes had taken place. Both cities were among a wide range of locations where Saudi Arabia announced alerts on Tuesday, although there were no similar announcements on Wednesday. Saudi officials and oil company Aramco did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment. READ MORE Earlier, Saree said the Houthis had also shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. No immediate evidence was presented. Saree said the Saudis had carried out as many as 450 air strikes on Yemen this week. Officials in the Saudi-backed government that controls southern Yemen have acknowledged that their forces and those of Saudi Arabia were conducting air strikes on Houthi positions, though Riyadh has not confirmed them. The Houthis have fired repeatedly into Saudi Arabia over the past week, causing alarms over cities in the south and west. An attack blamed on Iran-aligned fighters in Iraq last week also knocked out Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, the main route used to divert exports away from the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Riyadh said its air defences had shot down a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, an attack it said crossed a “red line” of threatening shrines sacred to all Muslims. Houthi spokesperson Saree denied the group had targeted Mecca, and said the Saudi reports were propaganda. The extension of the war into Yemen threatens to worsen the global energy supply shortage caused by the six-month-old US-Israeli war on Iran, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The price of Brent crude hovered around $108 a barrel on Wednesday, close to its highest level since May. Traders say a prolonged closure of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline could cut off as much as 4 per cent of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume, but US energy secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days. Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since 2015. The conflict had largely quietened under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and fired at southern areas in the kingdom. Violence has intensified sharply this month as the militant group pushed back forces aligned with the Saudi-backed internationally recognised Yemeni government. Saudi Arabia’s crown prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned US president Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so far has been limited to intelligence aid. The United States bombed the Houthis for two months in 2025, but halted that campaign after reaching what Trump described as a ceasefire with the group. Trump now faces a dilemma of whether to stand by and risk the Houthi advance worsening the global energy crisis, or provide more direct military support to the Saudis and risk extending the costly US intervention to another part of the Middle East. – Reuters

title: Today in Germany: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
description: Organised crime in Germany getting more international, digitally connected and violent, school pupils in Bavaria evacuated after chlorine gas leak, drone maker forced underground amid suspected Russian threat and more news on Wednesday.
content: Today's top story: Organised crime in Germany becoming more international and digitally connected Germany’s organised crime networks are becoming increasingly international, digitally connected and violent, according to the Federal Criminal Police Office's (BKA) latest report. The number of investigation proceedings into organised crime rose to 683 in 2025, the highest figure since 2021, while the number of suspects increased by more than 13 percent to 7,988 – also the highest level in five years. While presenting the findings, BKA Chief Holger Münch said: "Organised crime is changing its face: criminal networks today operate in a much more digitally interconnected, international and division-of-labour-based manner." Drug-related crime once again accounted for the vast majority of organised crime investigations during the reporting period, followed by economic crime, tax and customs offences, migrant smuggling, property crimes and money laundering. A total of 31 investigations focused primarily on violent crime. The BKA warned of an increase in extreme violence, including cases in which violent acts are commissioned as a service or carried out by minors recruited specifically for the purpose. Perpetrators are increasingly being recruited through social media, with some of those hired to carry out violent crimes as young as 13. Such criminal acts operate on the principle of "one plans, one pays, one carries out the attack," said Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) on Tuesday. Münch added that criminal networks today also "exploit geopolitical conflicts". READ ALSO: Which types of crime are rising in Germany? German drone maker goes underground amid suspected Russia threat Changing location every few weeks and constantly accompanied by body guards, the head of a German startup supplying drones to Ukraine has been forced into hiding due to a suspected Russian assassination plot. "Putin chose this path, and I have to accept that and respond accordingly," Stefan Thumann, CEO of German defence tech firm Donaustahl, told AFP in an interview from an undisclosed location. The 39-year believes that the saga will only end one of two ways – when "the Russian regime is toppled" or the Russians succeed in killing him, he said. Thumann is an outspoken supporter of Ukraine's war against President Vladimir Putin and a supplier of attack drones to Kyiv. Authorities first warned him last December that he could be in danger, he said. Soon after, "I was explicitly told that the threat comes from Russia and that a murder attempt on me is planned," he said. His life has been turned upside down by being forced to go underground, although he still manages to oversee his company's work. "I'm more or less completely isolated from the outside world," he said, adding that communication with family was "sporadic" and "only digital". Contacted by AFP, the interior ministry of the southern state of Bavaria – where Donaustahl is based – said it was aware of the case but declined to comment further, noting that it was under investigation by federal prosecutors. School pupils in Würzburg evacuated after gas leak Around 2,000 pupils were evacuated from a vocational school in Würzburg, Bavaria, on Tuesday due to a chlorine gas leak at the building's swimming pool. The incident happened shortly before 10am at the Franz-Oberthür School. Firefighters said two substances used to disinfect the pool had been combined – but because the swimming pool water was missing, the two agents triggered an unwanted chemical reaction. A total of 14 people were affected, with 10 taken to hospital mainly suffering from respiratory irritation. The fire service later gave the all-clear after emergency crews removed and neutralised the chemical mixture. Police are investigating the circumstances of the incident. German investor morale misses expectations as Mideast war weighs German investor sentiment rose much less than expected in September, a closely watched survey showed Tuesday, underscoring the economy's fragility as the Mideast war persists and suspected attacks on infrastructure unnerve investors. The ZEW institute's economic expectations index edged up just 0.5 points to 34.7, the survey found, its fifth rise in a row. That was far below forecasts of a 10-point increase in a poll of analysts by the financial platform FactSet. Expensive energy resulting from the US war against Iran and the near total closure of the Strait of Hormuz were weighing on sentiment, ZEW president Achim Wambach said. Petrol prices on Monday reached a record of €2.286 ($2.64) a litre in Germany as the war pushes up oil and gas prices worldwide. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Tuesday that the government "had to act" on fuel costs, adding that it would have concrete measures to announce "very soon". READ ALSO: Germany plans price relief for drivers amid rising fuel costs "The risks are nevertheless considerable," Wambach said, citing "high energy prices amid the ongoing war in Iran and further uncertainty caused by hybrid attacks are weighing on the economy". Berlin's run-down public spaces at heart of election campaign Politicians campaigning for Sunday's Berlin state election have painted an unflattering picture of the German capital, vowing to clear garbage-strewn streets and promising "syringe-free playgrounds". Town hall-hopefuls have also pledged to clean up graffiti-covered train stations, end "forever-building sites", fix buckled cycling lanes and take steps to ease a desperate shortage of affordable housing. Taken together, the list of woes hardens the image of a chronically broke city whose administration often struggles to reliably provide services for its almost four million people. READ ALSO: - Why is rubbish causing such a stink in the Berlin elections? - What foreign residents need to know about Berlin's upcoming election Certainly, many who live in Berlin love its rich artistic and cultural life, green spaces, lakes and children's playgrounds, vibrant start-up scene and hedonistic, anything-goes nightlife. But that has gone hand-in-hand with persistent complaints about a slow bureaucracy and dysfunctional services. Local newspapers often write about Berlin's "crime hotspots" and rising homelessness, and make great sport of documenting ever-new Berlin disasters – from rat-infested police stations to the closure of the Technical University's main campus due to structural defects and fire safety issues. A spokesperson for the City told AFP, when asked about the garbage problem, that there were "no operational failures", pointing instead to many residents' lack of civic responsibility. With reporting by AFP

title: Praj Industries inks development & commercialization agreement for bio-isobutanol with Gevo
description: Praj Industries said that it signed a development & commercialization agreement for bio-isobutanol (Bio-IBA) technology in India.
content: Praj Industries inks development & commercialization agreement for bio-isobutanol with Gevo Praj Industries said that it signed a development & commercialization agreement for bio-isobutanol (Bio-IBA) technology in India. Under the agreement, Praj will lead the commercialization of Bio-IBA technology in India, with exclusive rights to deploy the technology in the country. The partnership will focus on developing commercial opportunities for Bio-IBA, with primary emphasis on diesel blending applications that have the potential to reduce the carbon intensity of one of the worlds most widely used transportation and industrial fuels. In a separate development aligned with the broader objective of advancing Bio-IBA adoption, Praj is currently establishing India's first commercial Bio-IBA demonstration plant for a leading oil marketing company (OMC). The project is being designed, engineered, supplied and erected by Praj based on Gevo's licensed bio-IBA technology. Also Read The demonstration plant is expected to play an important role in validating production, supply chain and market-development pathways for future commercialization opportunities in India. Bio-IBA presents a promising opportunity for reducing the carbon footprint of diesel across a wide range of applications, including transportation, agriculture, mining, construction and industrial operations. Given India's large diesel economy and abundant renewable feedstock resources, Bio-IBA has the potential to become an important component in the country's transition towards lower-carbon fuels. Paul Bloom, chief executive officer, Gevo: "This agreement marks an important milestone in our relationship with Praj and in the advancement of Bio-IBA in India. Gevo brings proven renewable isobutanol technology and commercialization experience, while Praj contributes deep expertise in engineering, deployment and market development. Together, we are creating a framework to unlock new opportunities for Bio-IBA, particularly in diesel applications, while supporting broader decarbonization objectives." Praj Industries operates across three key business segments: bioenergy, hi-purity systems and engineering. The Bioenergy business focuses on process design, engineering, fabrication and commissioning of ethanol plants and. Hi-Purity Systems provides solutions for high-purity process applications. The Engineering business comprises water and wastewater treatment, critical process engineering and brewery plants and equipment, serving industries including oil & gas, petrochemicals, fertilisers, chemicals and brewing. The company had reported 117.42% increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 11.61 crore on a 11.81% rise in revenue to Rs 715.82 crore in Q1 FY27 as compared with Q1 FY26. The scrip fell 1.20% to currently trade at Rs 314.15 on the BSE.
